### gRPC Bidirectional Streaming with Back-Pressure and Controlled Close  [community]

k6's `k6/net/grpc` `Stream` API supports full bidirectional streaming. A common production
gotcha is failing to handle the `end` event correctly, leaving the stream open and causing
the VU to hang. The pattern below uses a `Promise`-wrapped event loop with a completion flag
to safely drain both send and receive sides.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/grpc-bidi-stream.js
import grpc   from "k6/net/grpc";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Counter, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const client            = new grpc.Client();
const streamMsgsReceived = new Counter("grpc_stream_msgs_received");
const streamRoundTrip    = new Trend("grpc_stream_round_trip_ms", true);

client.load(["./proto"], "routeguide.proto");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    bidi_stream: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 5,
      duration: "3m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    grpc_stream_round_trip_ms: ["p(95)<500"],
    grpc_stream_msgs_received: ["count>100"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  client.connect(__ENV.GRPC_ADDR || "localhost:50051", { plaintext: true });

  const sentAt   = {};
  let   streamDone = false;
  let   msgCount   = 0;

  const stream = new grpc.Stream(client, "routeguide.RouteGuide/RouteChat");

  // ── Receive side ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  stream.on("data", (note) => {
    const sent = sentAt[note.message];
    if (sent) {
      streamRoundTrip.add(Date.now() - sent);
      delete sentAt[note.message];
    }
    streamMsgsReceived.add(1);
    msgCount++;
  });

  stream.on("end", () => { streamDone = true; });

  stream.on("error", (e) => {
    console.error(`gRPC stream error: ${JSON.stringify(e)}`);
    streamDone = true;   // unblock the poll loop on error too
  });

  // ── Send side — write 10 messages then close ──────────────────────────────
  const points = generateRoutePoints(10);   // helper that returns Array<{location, message}>
  for (const point of points) {
    sentAt[point.message] = Date.now();
    stream.write(point);
    sleep(0.1);   // light throttle — avoid overwhelming the server buffer
  }
  stream.end();   // signal EOF; server will echo and close

  // ── Drain: poll until streamDone or timeout ───────────────────────────────
  const DEADLINE = Date.now() + 10_000;  // 10 s max wait
  while (!streamDone && Date.now() < DEADLINE) {
    sleep(0.05);
  }

  check(msgCount, { "all echoes received": (n) => n >= points.length });
  client.close();
  sleep(1);
}

function generateRoutePoints(count) {
  return Array.from({ length: count }, (_, i) => ({
    location: { latitude: 408009737, longitude: -748763950 + i * 1000 },
    message: `ping-${__VU}-${__ITER}-${i}`,
  }));
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #97:** Always call `stream.end()` in a `finally` block for client-streaming
> and bidirectional streams. If the VU errors before reaching `stream.end()`, the server-side
> stream never closes, consuming a server goroutine until the k6 test ends. Use:
> ```javascript
> try { /* write messages */ } finally { stream.end(); }
> ```

### `k6/secrets` Module — Secure Credential Injection with `--secret-source`  (k6 v1.5+)

The `k6/secrets` built-in module provides an async `get()` API that retrieves secrets from
configured sources without exposing them in environment variables, CLI args, or k6 logs.
Secrets are automatically redacted as `***SECRET_REDACTED***` in all console output.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/secrets-auth.js — k6/secrets module usage
import secrets   from "k6/secrets";
import http      from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    auth_test: {
      executor: "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate: 5, timeUnit: "1s", duration: "5m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 10,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(99)<1000"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.005"],
  },
};

// setup() is the correct place to fetch secrets — runs once, not per-VU-iteration
export async function setup() {
  // secrets.get() uses the DEFAULT source (configured via --secret-source flag)
  const apiKey    = await secrets.get("API_KEY");
  const apiSecret = await secrets.get("API_SECRET");

  // Verify we got values (secrets.get returns undefined if key not found)
  if (!apiKey || !apiSecret) {
    throw new Error("Required secrets API_KEY or API_SECRET not found in secret source");
  }

  // Exchange for a short-lived JWT — only the JWT is distributed to VUs
  const tokenRes = http.post(`${__ENV.AUTH_URL}/token`, JSON.stringify({
    key: apiKey, secret: apiSecret,
  }), { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });

  check(tokenRes, { "token obtained": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  return { jwt: tokenRes.json("access_token"), expiresIn: tokenRes.json("expires_in") };
}

export default function (data) {
  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/protected`, {
    headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${data.jwt}` },
  });
  check(res, { "authorized": (r) => r.status === 200 });
}
```

**`--secret-source` configuration options:**

```bash
# Mock source (testing / local dev — never in production CI)
k6 run --secret-source=mock=default,API_KEY="local-key",API_SECRET="local-secret" script.js

# HashiCorp Vault (URL-based, k6 v1.5+ url:// schema)
k6 run --secret-source=url=https://vault.example.com/v1/secret/data/k6 script.js

# Environment alias (K6_SECRET_SOURCE env var, k6 v1.7+)
export K6_SECRET_SOURCE="mock=default,API_KEY=ci-key"
k6 run script.js

# k6 Cloud auto-injection — secrets in Grafana Cloud are auto-injected
# when running with --local-execution; opt out with --no-cloud-secrets
k6 cloud run --local-execution --no-cloud-secrets script.js
```

> **[community] Gotcha #98:** `secrets.get()` is **async** — it returns a Promise, not a value.
> Calling it without `await` silently passes a `Promise` object as the secret value, causing
> authentication failures with no obvious error. Always `await` in an `async` function:
> `const key = await secrets.get("MY_KEY");`

> **[community] Gotcha #99:** `secrets.get()` inside `default()` creates one network/IPC call
> per VU per iteration to the secret source. For a 100-VU, 10-minute test this can be
> thousands of calls. Fetch secrets in `setup()` and pass them to VUs via the return value, or
> use a module-level cache initialized on first call:
> ```javascript
> let _cachedKey;
> async function getApiKey() {
>   if (!_cachedKey) _cachedKey = await secrets.get("API_KEY");
>   return _cachedKey;
> }
> ```
> Module-level caching is per-VU (each VU has its own JS runtime), so the cache makes at most
> `vus` calls to the secret source rather than `vus × iterations`.

---

### OpenTelemetry Output: Rate Metric Format Change (k6 v1.4+) and Grafana Tempo Integration

k6's `--out opentelemetry` exports metrics to any OTEL-compatible collector. Starting in
v1.4.0, `Rate` metrics changed from a single gauge to a counter with `condition` attribute.
This section covers both the full integration setup and the breaking-change dashboard migration.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/otel-traced-load-test.js — correlate k6 metrics with distributed traces
import http       from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep }  from "k6";
import { Counter, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

// Custom metrics exported to OTEL
const traceErrors = new Counter("trace_errors_total");
const e2eLatency  = new Trend("e2e_latency_ms", true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    traced_checkout: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 20,
      duration: "10m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    e2e_latency_ms:    ["p(95)<2000"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  // Inject trace context headers manually for correlation with app traces
  const traceId   = generateTraceId();
  const spanId    = generateSpanId();
  const traceHeaders = {
    "traceparent": `00-${traceId}-${spanId}-01`,
    "X-Load-Test": "true",
  };

  const start    = Date.now();
  const cartRes  = http.post(`${__ENV.CART_URL}/add`,
    JSON.stringify({ productId: "p-123", qty: 1 }),
    { headers: { ...traceHeaders, "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
  );
  const orderRes = http.post(`${__ENV.ORDER_URL}/checkout`,
    JSON.stringify({ cartId: cartRes.json("cartId") }),
    { headers: { ...traceHeaders, "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
  );
  e2eLatency.add(Date.now() - start);

  const ok = check(orderRes, {
    "order placed":    (r) => r.status === 201,
    "has confirmation": (r) => !!r.json("confirmationId"),
  });
  if (!ok) traceErrors.add(1);
  sleep(1);
}

// Minimal trace ID generators (hex strings, not cryptographically secure)
function generateTraceId() {
  return Array.from({ length: 32 }, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 16).toString(16)).join("");
}
function generateSpanId() {
  return Array.from({ length: 16 }, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 16).toString(16)).join("");
}
```

**Run with OTEL output to local Grafana Alloy / Tempo:**

```bash
# Send to local OTEL collector
k6 run \
  --out opentelemetry \
  --env K6_OTEL_GRPC_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT=localhost:4317 \
  --env K6_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=k6-load-test \
  --env K6_OTEL_SERVICE_VERSION=1.0.0 \
  script.js
```

**PromQL for Rate metrics (v1.4+ format):**

```promql
# k6 http_req_failed rate (v1.4+ dual-counter format)
rate(k6_http_req_failed_total{condition="nonzero"}[1m]) /
(
  rate(k6_http_req_failed_total{condition="nonzero"}[1m]) +
  rate(k6_http_req_failed_total{condition="zero"}[1m])
)

# Custom Rate metric (same pattern)
rate(k6_trace_errors_total{condition="nonzero"}[1m]) /
(rate(k6_trace_errors_total{condition="nonzero"}[1m]) + rate(k6_trace_errors_total{condition="zero"}[1m]))
```

> **[community] Gotcha #100:** When upgrading from k6 < v1.4.0 to v1.4.0+, existing OTEL-based
> Grafana dashboards that query rate metrics as single gauges will show **no data** after the
> upgrade. Update all panels that reference `k6_*_rate` gauge metrics to use the new dual-counter
> PromQL pattern above. The change affects ALL `Rate` metric types — both built-in (e.g.,
> `http_req_failed`) and custom ones you created with `new Rate(...)`.

### `handleSummary` with JUnit XML + Slack Webhook — Dual-Output CI Pattern

`handleSummary()` can write to **multiple destinations simultaneously** by returning an object
with multiple keys. This pattern emits a JUnit XML file (for CI test reports) and sends a Slack
notification in the same function call, with no external tooling required.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/lib/summary.js — reusable multi-output handleSummary
import { textSummary } from "https://jslib.k6.io/k6-summary/0.0.2/index.js";
import { jUnit }       from "https://jslib.k6.io/k6-summary/0.0.2/index.js";
import http            from "k6/http";

/**
 * Multi-output handleSummary:
 * - writes junit.xml for CI test result ingestion
 * - writes summary.json for downstream tooling
 * - POSTs to Slack if SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL env var is set
 * - always prints a human-readable summary to stdout
 */
export function buildHandleSummary(slackChannel = "#load-tests") {
  return function handleSummary(data) {
    const outputs = {
      "stdout":       textSummary(data, { indent: "  ", enableColors: true }),
      "junit.xml":    jUnit(data),
      "summary.json": JSON.stringify(data, null, 2),
    };

    // Slack notification — only if webhook is configured
    if (__ENV.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL) {
      const passedThresholds = Object.entries(data.metrics)
        .filter(([, m]) => m.thresholds)
        .every(([, m]) => Object.values(m.thresholds).every((t) => t.ok));

      const status   = passedThresholds ? ":white_check_mark: PASSED" : ":x: FAILED";
      const p95      = data.metrics.http_req_duration?.values?.["p(95)"]?.toFixed(0) ?? "N/A";
      const errRate  = ((data.metrics.http_req_failed?.values?.rate ?? 0) * 100).toFixed(2);
      const testName = __ENV.TEST_NAME || "k6 Load Test";

      http.post(__ENV.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, JSON.stringify({
        channel: slackChannel,
        text: `${status} *${testName}*\n• p95: ${p95}ms  • error rate: ${errRate}%\n• VUs: ${data.metrics.vus_max?.values?.max ?? "?"}`,
      }), { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } });
    }

    return outputs;
  };
}
```

```javascript
// k6/scripts/load-test.js — use the shared handleSummary
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { buildHandleSummary } from "./lib/summary.js";

export const options = {
  stages: [
    { target: 50, duration: "2m" },
    { target: 50, duration: "5m" },
    { target: 0,  duration: "1m" },
  ],
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.02"],
  },
};

export const handleSummary = buildHandleSummary("#perf-alerts");

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.BASE_URL}/api/health`);
  check(res, { "healthy": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #101:** The `textSummary()` function from jslib prints ALL metrics by
> default, including `data_received`, `data_sent`, `iteration_duration`, etc. For dashboards
> where only business metrics matter, delete the noisy built-in keys before passing to
> `textSummary()`:
> ```javascript
> const NOISE = ["data_received","data_sent","iteration_duration","iterations","vus","vus_max"];
> NOISE.forEach((k) => delete data.metrics[k]);
> return { stdout: textSummary(data, { indent: "  " }) };
> ```

### `page.route()` Mocking Pattern — Stub External APIs in Browser Tests

Mocking network requests in k6 browser tests with `page.route()` keeps tests hermetic by
intercepting calls to third-party APIs (analytics, payment providers, feature flags) and
returning synthetic responses. This prevents flaky tests caused by external service downtime
and removes test data from production analytics systems.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/browser-route-mock.js — mock external APIs in browser test
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check }   from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    checkout_mocked: {
      executor: "shared-iterations",
      vus: 2,
      iterations: 4,
      options: { browser: { type: "chromium" } },
    },
  },
  thresholds: { checks: ["rate==1.0"] },
};

const APP = __ENV.APP_URL || "http://localhost:3000";

export default async function () {
  const page = await browser.newPage();

  try {
    // ── Block analytics to prevent test data pollution ────────────────────
    await page.route("**/analytics/**", async (route) => {
      await route.abort();   // drop the request; no error shown to page
    });

    // ── Stub payment provider to return a predictable success response ────
    await page.route("**/api/payment/process", async (route) => {
      await route.fulfill({
        status: 200,
        contentType: "application/json",
        body: JSON.stringify({ transactionId: "test-txn-001", status: "approved" }),
      });
    });

    // ── Intercept but modify (add header) for feature-flag API ───────────
    await page.route("**/api/features", async (route) => {
      await route.continue({
        headers: {
          ...route.request().headers(),
          "X-Feature-Override": "checkout-v2=enabled",
        },
      });
    });

    await page.goto(`${APP}/checkout`);
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Place Order" }).click();

    const confirmation = page.getByTestId("order-confirmation");
    await confirmation.waitFor({ state: "visible" });

    check(await confirmation.textContent(), {
      "confirmation shown": (t) => t.includes("Order confirmed"),
    });

  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

**Route action comparison:**

| Action | Effect | Use when |
|--------|--------|---------|
| `route.abort()` | Request fails (network error in browser) | Blocking ads, trackers, analytics |
| `route.fulfill({...})` | Custom synthetic response returned | Mocking APIs, stable test data |
| `route.continue({...})` | Request proceeds with optional overrides | Adding headers, modifying body |

> **[community] Gotcha #102:** Only the **last registered handler** for a matching URL runs.
> Registering two `page.route()` calls for the same pattern is a silent bug — the first handler
> never executes. If you need to intercept the same URL for different purposes in the same test,
> compose both actions inside a single handler function.

> **[community] Gotcha #103:** `page.route()` accepts **glob patterns and exact URL strings only**
> (not regex). Passing a regex literal like `/\/api\/payment/` silently never matches any URL.
> Use glob syntax: `"**/api/payment/**"`.

---

### Threshold Strategy: SLO-Tiered Thresholds with `abortOnFail` and `delayAbortEval`

Production SLOs typically have multiple levels: a hard threshold (abort the test immediately)
and a soft threshold (report but continue). This pattern encodes both in a single thresholds
config, with carefully tuned `delayAbortEval` to prevent premature termination during ramp-up.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/slo-tiered-thresholds.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Rate, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const checkoutErrors = new Rate("checkout_error_rate");
const checkoutLatency = new Trend("checkout_latency_ms", true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    steady_load: {
      executor: "ramping-arrival-rate",
      startRate: 5,
      timeUnit: "1s",
      stages: [
        { target: 20, duration: "2m" },   // ramp up
        { target: 20, duration: "10m" },  // sustain
        { target: 0,  duration: "2m" },   // ramp down
      ],
      preAllocatedVUs: 30,
      maxVUs: 60,
    },
  },

  thresholds: {
    // ── HTTP infrastructure — hard abort if catastrophic ──────────────────
    http_req_failed: [
      // Soft: warn if error rate > 1%
      "rate<0.01",
      // Hard: abort immediately if error rate > 5%
      { threshold: "rate<0.05", abortOnFail: true, delayAbortEval: "30s" },
    ],

    // ── Checkout SLO: p95 < 500ms (warn); p99 < 1s (hard abort after 1m) ─
    checkout_latency_ms: [
      "p(95)<500",
      "p(99)<1000",
      { threshold: "p(99)<2000", abortOnFail: true, delayAbortEval: "1m" },
    ],

    // ── Business metric: checkout success rate ────────────────────────────
    checkout_error_rate: [
      "rate<0.02",
      { threshold: "rate<0.10", abortOnFail: true, delayAbortEval: "30s" },
    ],

    // ── Minimum throughput gate: test data is meaningless below 100 req/s ─
    "http_reqs": ["rate>100"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const start = Date.now();
  const res = http.post(`${__ENV.CHECKOUT_URL}/api/checkout`,
    JSON.stringify({ cartId: `cart-${__VU}`, items: [{ sku: "ABC", qty: 1 }] }),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
  );
  checkoutLatency.add(Date.now() - start);

  const ok = check(res, {
    "checkout 200": (r) => r.status === 200,
    "has orderId":  (r) => !!r.json("orderId"),
  });
  checkoutErrors.add(!ok);
  sleep(0.5);
}
```

**`delayAbortEval` tuning guide:**

| Ramp phase | Recommended `delayAbortEval` | Reason |
|------------|------------------------------|--------|
| 0–30 s (startup) | `"30s"` | Cold-start latency spikes inflate p99 |
| 30 s–5 min (ramp) | `"1m"` | Traffic not yet at target; percentiles misleading |
| Steady state | `"15s"` | Detect genuine SLO breaches quickly |
| Soak test (> 1 h) | `"5m"` | Avoid abort on transient GC pauses |

> **[community] Gotcha #104:** Thresholds on **custom metrics** (`new Rate`, `new Trend`) only
> include data collected **up to the point `handleSummary` runs** — which is after `teardown()`.
> If a custom metric is only updated in `teardown()`, its threshold evaluation sees all values.
> However, if you update a custom metric inside `setup()`, that value is **NOT included** in
> threshold evaluation (setup() runs in a separate evaluation context). Validate custom metrics
> that must trigger aborts in `default()`, not `setup()`/`teardown()`.

### `k6/experimental/streams` — Memory-Efficient Large CSV Processing  (k6 v1.4+)

The `k6/experimental/streams` module provides a `ReadableStream` API for processing large
files chunk-by-chunk rather than loading them entirely into memory. Combined with
`k6/experimental/fs`, this enables multi-GB CSV corpora without OOM errors.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/stream-csv-vudata.js — stream a large CSV file, fan out to VUs
import { open }         from "k6/experimental/fs";
import { SharedArray }  from "k6/data";
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

// SharedArray is populated via streaming in the module init phase
// This approach uses ReadableStream line-by-line to avoid loading full file
const USER_RECORDS = new SharedArray("users_stream", async function* () {
  const file     = await open("./data/users-large.csv");
  const decoder  = new TextDecoder();
  let   leftover = "";
  let   isHeader = true;

  // Read the file in 64 KB chunks
  const CHUNK = 65_536;
  const buf   = new Uint8Array(CHUNK);
  let   bytesRead;

  while ((bytesRead = await file.read(buf)) !== null) {
    leftover += decoder.decode(buf.subarray(0, bytesRead), { stream: true });
    const lines = leftover.split("\n");
    leftover    = lines.pop();   // incomplete last line carried forward

    for (const line of lines) {
      if (!line.trim()) continue;
      if (isHeader) { isHeader = false; continue; }   // skip CSV header row

      const [userId, email, role, region] = line.split(",");
      yield { userId: userId.trim(), email: email.trim(), role: role.trim(), region: region.trim() };
    }
  }

  // Flush any remaining partial line
  if (leftover.trim() && !isHeader) {
    const [userId, email, role, region] = leftover.split(",");
    yield { userId: userId.trim(), email: email.trim(), role: role.trim(), region: region.trim() };
  }
});

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    large_dataset: {
      executor: "per-vu-iterations",
      vus: 50,
      iterations: 100,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<600"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const user = USER_RECORDS[(__VU - 1 + __ITER) % USER_RECORDS.length];

  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/users/${user.userId}`, {
    tags: { role: user.role, region: user.region },
  });
  check(res, {
    "user found": (r) => r.status === 200,
    "role match": (r) => r.json("role") === user.role,
  });
  sleep(0.5);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #105:** `SharedArray` with an `async function*` generator works
> **only in k6 v1.4+**. In earlier versions, the generator is treated as a synchronous
> function and the yielded values are lost. Use `csv.parse()` with `SharedArray` for
> files under 50 MB if you need to support older k6 versions.

> **[community] Gotcha #106:** `file.read(buf)` returns `null` at EOF — not `0` or an
> empty buffer. Checking `bytesRead === 0` will loop infinitely at EOF. The correct
> EOF check is `bytesRead === null`.

### `mcp-k6` AI-Assisted Script Authoring (k6 v1.6+ Experimental)

`mcp-k6` is an official Grafana experimental MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that
integrates k6 into AI-assisted editors (VS Code Copilot, Claude, Cursor). It can generate
scripts from natural language, validate existing scripts, and run them locally.

```bash
# Install and configure mcp-k6 for VS Code / Claude Code
npx @grafana/k6-mcp-server install

# Capabilities exposed to the AI:
# - k6_generate_script: generate a k6 script from a prompt
# - k6_validate_script: validate syntax and k6 API usage
# - k6_run_script: execute a script locally and return summary JSON
# - k6_get_results: retrieve results from a previous run
```

```javascript
// Example: ask the AI to generate a script for a specific load scenario
// Prompt to AI: "Create a k6 script that tests my login API at /api/auth/login
// using POST with email/password from a CSV file, targeting p95 < 300ms,
// with a 5-minute ramp from 0 to 50 VUs then 10 minutes steady state"

// mcp-k6 generates (simplified output):
import http           from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { SharedArray }  from "k6/data";
import { parse }        from "k6/x/csv";   // or open() + csv.parse()

const CREDS = new SharedArray("creds", () => parse(open("./data/creds.csv")));

export const options = {
  stages: [
    { target: 50, duration: "5m" },
    { target: 50, duration: "10m" },
    { target: 0,  duration: "2m" },
  ],
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<300"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const cred = CREDS[__VU % CREDS.length];
  const res  = http.post(`${__ENV.BASE_URL}/api/auth/login`,
    JSON.stringify({ email: cred.email, password: cred.password }),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
  );
  check(res, {
    "login 200":     (r) => r.status === 200,
    "has auth token": (r) => !!r.json("token"),
  });
  sleep(Math.random() + 0.5);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #107:** `mcp-k6` is still experimental as of k6 v1.6. Generated
> scripts may reference extension modules (`k6/x/*`) that are not available in the official
> k6 binary. Always validate generated scripts against your actual k6 binary with
> `k6 inspect <script.js>` before running. The `k6_validate_script` MCP tool performs
> syntax checks but does not verify extension availability.

---

### `k6 deps` CLI — Script Dependency Analysis and Archive Inspection  (k6 v1.6+)

`k6 deps` analyzes a k6 script or archive and outputs all dependencies (local modules,
remote imports, extensions) as JSON. Use it in CI pipelines to enforce allowed-module
policies and detect unexpected remote imports that could introduce supply-chain risk.

```bash
# Analyze a script's dependencies
k6 deps script.js

# JSON output (pipe to jq for filtering)
k6 deps --output=json script.js | jq '.imports[] | select(.type == "remote")'

# Analyze a compiled archive
k6 deps my-test.tar.gz

# CI: fail the pipeline if any remote imports are detected
k6 deps --output=json script.js | jq -e '[.imports[] | select(.type == "remote")] | length == 0'
```

```javascript
// Example output structure from k6 deps --output=json
{
  "version": "1.6.0",
  "entrypoint": "script.js",
  "imports": [
    { "path": "k6/http",             "type": "builtin"   },
    { "path": "k6/data",             "type": "builtin"   },
    { "path": "./lib/summary.js",    "type": "local",    "resolved": "/tests/lib/summary.js" },
    { "path": "k6/x/faker",         "type": "extension" },
    {
      "path": "https://jslib.k6.io/k6-summary/0.0.2/index.js",
      "type": "remote",
      "hash": "sha256-abc123..."      // hash for integrity verification
    }
  ]
}
```

```yaml
# GitHub Actions: enforce no unreviewed remote imports
- name: Audit k6 dependencies
  run: |
    REMOTE=$(k6 deps --output=json scripts/checkout.js | \
      jq '[.imports[] | select(.type == "remote") | .path] | @tsv')
    APPROVED="https://jslib.k6.io/k6-summary/0.0.2/index.js"
    if echo "$REMOTE" | grep -vF "$APPROVED" | grep -q '.'; then
      echo "Unapproved remote k6 import detected!"
      exit 1
    fi
```

> **[community] Gotcha #108:** `k6 deps` resolves **static** imports only. Dynamic imports
> constructed at runtime (e.g., `import(someVariable)`) are not detected. If your scripts
> use dynamic extension loading, `k6 deps` will silently under-report dependencies.

---

### HTTP/2 Protocol Verification and `r.proto` Assertions

k6 automatically upgrades connections to HTTP/2 when the server supports it. However, in
performance testing it is important to **verify** that HTTP/2 was actually negotiated —
a misconfigured load balancer can silently downgrade to HTTP/1.1, invalidating your
multiplexing assumptions.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/http2-verify.js — assert HTTP protocol version per request
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, group, sleep } from "k6";
import { Counter } from "k6/metrics";

const http2Downgrades = new Counter("http2_downgrade_total");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    http2_test: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 10,
      duration: "5m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration:     ["p(95)<300"],
    http2_downgrade_total: ["count==0"],   // zero tolerance for HTTP/1.1 downgrades
  },
};

export default function () {
  group("HTTP/2 endpoint verification", () => {
    const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/products`, {
      tags: { endpoint: "products" },
    });

    const isHttp2 = check(res, {
      "status 200":    (r) => r.status === 200,
      // r.proto values: "HTTP/1.0", "HTTP/1.1", "HTTP/2.0"
      "uses HTTP/2":   (r) => r.proto === "HTTP/2.0",
      "response fast": (r) => r.timings.duration < 300,
    });

    // Track downgrades as a custom metric for threshold enforcement
    if (res.proto !== "HTTP/2.0") {
      http2Downgrades.add(1);
      console.warn(`HTTP/2 downgrade detected on VU ${__VU}: proto=${res.proto}`);
    }
  });

  sleep(0.5);
}
```

**h2c (HTTP/2 Cleartext) — when TLS is not available:**

```javascript
// h2c requires explicit opt-in via http2-prior-knowledge
// k6 does NOT yet support the HTTP/2 upgrade header (Upgrade: h2c)
// For h2c testing, configure the server to require h2c and check proto:
const res = http.get("http://internal-service:8080/api/data");  // no TLS
// k6 will use HTTP/1.1 unless the server advertises h2c via ALPN on TLS
// True h2c without TLS is only possible with k6 compiled with h2c support (xk6)
```

> **[community] Gotcha #109:** k6 uses a **shared** HTTP/2 connection pool per host per VU.
> Unlike browsers, k6 does not multiplex requests from multiple VUs over the same TCP
> connection. Each VU maintains its own connection pool. If you have 100 VUs all hitting
> the same host, k6 opens up to 100 TCP connections — not 1 multiplexed HTTP/2 connection.
> This is often more load than a browser-like scenario but accurately reflects server-side
> API client behavior.

### Web Vitals Measurement with k6 Browser Module  (k6 v1.5+)

k6 browser automatically collects Core Web Vitals as built-in metrics when using the
`k6/browser` module. Understanding the metric names and thresholds helps you write
meaningful performance assertions for browser-based flows.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/browser-web-vitals.js — measure and assert on Core Web Vitals
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check }   from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    vitals_test: {
      executor: "shared-iterations",
      vus: 3,
      iterations: 10,
      options: { browser: { type: "chromium" } },
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    // Core Web Vitals thresholds (Google "Good" benchmarks)
    browser_web_vital_lcp:  ["p(75)<2500"],   // Largest Contentful Paint < 2.5 s
    browser_web_vital_fcp:  ["p(75)<1800"],   // First Contentful Paint < 1.8 s
    browser_web_vital_cls:  ["p(75)<0.1"],    // Cumulative Layout Shift < 0.1
    browser_web_vital_inp:  ["p(75)<200"],    // Interaction to Next Paint < 200 ms
    browser_web_vital_ttfb: ["p(75)<800"],    // Time to First Byte < 800 ms

    // Browser-based request duration (heavier than HTTP-only due to rendering)
    browser_http_req_duration: ["p(95)<3000"],
  },
};

const PAGES = [
  { name: "home",     path: "/" },
  { name: "products", path: "/products" },
  { name: "cart",     path: "/cart" },
];

export default async function () {
  const pageConfig = PAGES[__ITER % PAGES.length];
  const page       = await browser.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto(`${__ENV.APP_URL}${pageConfig.path}`, {
      waitUntil: "networkidle",
    });

    // Web Vitals are collected automatically — no explicit measurement needed.
    // Trigger user interaction to measure INP (replaces FID in k6 v2.0+):
    const mainContent = page.getByRole("main");
    if (await mainContent.count() > 0) {
      await mainContent.click();
    }

    check(page, {
      "page title set": async (p) => (await p.title()).length > 0,
    });
  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

**Built-in browser metric reference:**

| Metric name | Web Vital | "Good" threshold | Notes |
|-------------|-----------|-----------------|-------|
| `browser_web_vital_lcp` | LCP | < 2500 ms | Largest visible element rendered |
| `browser_web_vital_fcp` | FCP | < 1800 ms | First DOM content painted |
| `browser_web_vital_cls` | CLS | < 0.1 | Layout shift score (unitless) |
| `browser_web_vital_inp` | INP | < 200 ms | Interaction to Next Paint (v2.0+) |
| `browser_web_vital_ttfb` | TTFB | < 800 ms | Time to first server byte |
| ~~`browser_web_vital_fid`~~ | FID | deprecated | Replaced by INP in k6 v2.0 |

> **[community] Gotcha #110:** `browser_web_vital_fid` was renamed to `browser_web_vital_inp`
> in k6 v2.0.0. Thresholds referencing `browser_web_vital_fid` silently have **no effect**
> after upgrading — the metric name no longer exists and k6 does not warn about unknown
> threshold keys. Always update threshold configs when upgrading k6 major versions.

### `execution.scenario.iterationInTest` — Globally Unique Iteration IDs for Distributed Tracing

When running distributed tests with multiple k6 instances, each instance has its own `__ITER`
counter starting from 0. Use `execution.scenario.iterationInTest` for a globally unique
iteration number that is consistent across all instances.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/distributed-trace-ids.js — unique IDs across distributed k6 nodes
import { execution }  from "k6";
import http           from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    purchase_flow: {
      executor: "shared-iterations",
      vus: 50,
      iterations: 10_000,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const scenarioCtx = execution.scenario;
  const vuCtx       = execution.vu;

  // ── Globally unique iteration ID ─────────────────────────────────────────
  // iterationInTest is unique across all VUs and all k6 instances
  // __ITER is per-VU; vuCtx.idInTest is per-VU globally unique
  const globalIterationId = `${scenarioCtx.name}-${scenarioCtx.iterationInTest}`;
  const globalVuId        = `vu-${vuCtx.idInTest}`;

  // Annotate all metrics for this iteration with the global IDs
  execution.vu.metrics.tags["iterationId"] = globalIterationId;
  execution.vu.metrics.tags["vuId"]        = globalVuId;

  // Use the global iteration ID as a correlation ID in request headers
  const res = http.post(
    `${__ENV.API_URL}/purchase`,
    JSON.stringify({ orderId: globalIterationId, productSku: "WIDGET-001" }),
    {
      headers: {
        "Content-Type": "application/json",
        "X-Correlation-ID": globalIterationId,  // traceable in server logs
        "X-Load-Test-VU":   globalVuId,
      },
    }
  );

  check(res, {
    "purchase accepted": (r) => r.status === 202,
    "correlation echoed": (r) => r.headers["X-Correlation-ID"] === globalIterationId,
  });

  // Use scenarioCtx.progress (0–1) for time-aware test logic
  if (scenarioCtx.progress < 0.1) {
    // First 10% of test — extra sleep for warm-up stabilization
    sleep(2);
  } else {
    sleep(0.5);
  }
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #111:** `execution.scenario.iterationInTest` is **not globally unique
> across scenarios**. If you have two scenarios in your `options.scenarios` config, each
> has its own counter starting from 0. For cross-scenario uniqueness, combine scenario name
> with iteration number: `` `${execution.scenario.name}-${execution.scenario.iterationInTest}` ``.

### Native TypeScript Support (k6 v0.57+) — `esbuild` Transpilation and `@types/k6`

Since k6 v0.57, TypeScript files (`.ts` extension) are transpiled automatically by the
built-in esbuild integration — no Webpack/Rollup step required for simple scripts. However,
esbuild **strips types only** — it does not type-check. Run `tsc --noEmit` separately for
safety.

```typescript
// k6/scripts/typed-check.ts — TypeScript native support with @types/k6
// Install: npm install -D @types/k6
// Run: k6 run typed-check.ts  (no build step needed in k6 v0.57+)
// Type-check: npx tsc --noEmit  (run separately — esbuild does NOT type-check)

import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import type { Options } from "k6/options";
import type { RefinedResponse, ResponseType } from "k6/http";

// Typed options — TypeScript will enforce valid executor/threshold syntax
export const options: Options = {
  scenarios: {
    load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 20 },
        { duration: "1m",  target: 20 },
        { duration: "10s", target: 0  },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<400"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

// Typed helper — response type parameter narrows body access
function assertJsonField<T>(
  res: RefinedResponse<ResponseType>,
  field: string,
): T | undefined {
  try {
    const body = res.json() as Record<string, T>;
    return body[field];
  } catch {
    return undefined;
  }
}

export default function (): void {
  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/products`);

  check(res, {
    "status 200":    (r) => r.status === 200,
    "has products":  (r) => (assertJsonField<unknown[]>(r, "items")?.length ?? 0) > 0,
  });

  sleep(1);
}
```

**TypeScript bundler decision table:**

| Scenario | Recommended approach |
|----------|---------------------|
| Simple single-file script | k6 native TS (v0.57+): `k6 run script.ts` |
| Multiple local modules | k6 native TS with relative imports — works out of the box |
| npm packages (axios, lodash, faker) | Webpack/Rollup bundle step — k6 native TS cannot resolve `node_modules` |
| Monorepo shared library | Rollup + path aliases in `tsconfig.json` + bundle |
| Type safety CI gate | Always add `npx tsc --noEmit` as a separate pre-run step |

> **[community] Gotcha #112:** k6's esbuild transpiler **silently ignores TypeScript errors**.
> A script with a wrong type annotation runs without warning. Add `npx tsc --noEmit` to
> your CI pipeline before `k6 run` so type errors surface as CI failures, not silent
> runtime bugs.

### `grpc.Client.asyncInvoke()` — Non-Blocking Unary gRPC Calls  (k6 v1.4+)

`asyncInvoke()` is the async counterpart to `invoke()`. It returns a `Promise` that resolves
to the same `Response` object, allowing `await` syntax and enabling concurrent unary calls
from a single VU without blocking.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/grpc-async-invoke.js — concurrent gRPC unary calls per VU
import grpc   from "k6/net/grpc";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const client             = new grpc.Client();
const ratingCallDuration = new Trend("grpc_rating_call_ms", true);
const priceCallDuration  = new Trend("grpc_price_call_ms", true);

client.load(["./proto"], "catalog.proto");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    concurrent_calls: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 10,
      duration: "2m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    grpc_rating_call_ms: ["p(95)<200"],
    grpc_price_call_ms:  ["p(95)<150"],
  },
};

export function setup() {
  client.connect(__ENV.GRPC_ADDR || "api.example.com:50051", {
    plaintext: false,
    timeout: "5s",
  });
}

export default async function () {
  const sku = `PROD-${(__VU * 100) + __ITER % 100}`;

  // ── Fire two unary calls concurrently with Promise.all ────────────────────
  const [ratingRes, priceRes] = await Promise.all([
    (async () => {
      const t0  = Date.now();
      const res = await client.asyncInvoke("catalog.CatalogService/GetRating", { sku });
      ratingCallDuration.add(Date.now() - t0);
      return res;
    })(),
    (async () => {
      const t0  = Date.now();
      const res = await client.asyncInvoke("catalog.CatalogService/GetPrice", { sku });
      priceCallDuration.add(Date.now() - t0);
      return res;
    })(),
  ]);

  check(ratingRes, { "rating OK": (r) => r.status === grpc.StatusOK });
  check(priceRes,  { "price OK":  (r) => r.status === grpc.StatusOK });

  sleep(0.5);
}

export function teardown() {
  client.close();
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #113:** `asyncInvoke()` **requires the script's default export to be
> an `async function`**. Mixing `async default()` with synchronous VU loops works fine, but
> if you call `await client.asyncInvoke()` inside a non-async default function, k6 silently
> converts the Promise to `undefined` — the response is never awaited and checks always pass
> vacuously. Always declare `export default async function ()` when using any `await`.

---

### `grpc.Client.healthCheck()` — Standardized Service Health Verification  (k6 v1.4+)

`healthCheck(service, params)` implements the [gRPC Health Checking Protocol](https://github.com/grpc/grpc/blob/master/doc/health-checking.md).
It calls `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check` and returns a response with `.status` equal to
`grpc.StatusOK` and a body containing the service's `servingStatus` (`SERVING`, `NOT_SERVING`, etc.).
Use it in `setup()` to gate the test on readiness, avoiding load against an unhealthy target.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/grpc-health-gate.js — abort test if service is unhealthy
import grpc from "k6/net/grpc";
import { check } from "k6";

const client = new grpc.Client();
client.load(["./proto"], "order-service.proto");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    load: {
      executor: "ramping-arrival-rate",
      startRate: 10,
      timeUnit: "1s",
      stages: [
        { target: 100, duration: "2m" },
        { target: 100, duration: "5m" },
        { target: 0,   duration: "30s" },
      ],
      preAllocatedVUs: 50,
      maxVUs: 150,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_failed: ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export function setup() {
  client.connect(__ENV.GRPC_ADDR || "order-service:50051", { plaintext: true });

  // ── Health gate: abort test if service is not ready ───────────────────────
  const health = client.healthCheck("order.OrderService");

  if (health.status !== grpc.StatusOK) {
    throw new Error(
      `gRPC healthCheck failed with status ${health.status} — aborting load test`
    );
  }

  const servingStatus = health.message?.status;
  if (servingStatus !== "SERVING") {
    throw new Error(
      `Service is ${servingStatus}, expected SERVING — aborting load test`
    );
  }

  console.log(`gRPC health check passed: ${servingStatus}`);
  return { healthChecked: true };
}

export default function () {
  // ... test logic using the healthy service ...
}

export function teardown() {
  client.close();
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #114:** `healthCheck()` requires the target service to implement the
> gRPC Health Checking Protocol (i.e., `grpc.health.v1.Health/Check`). Calling it against a
> service that does not register a health handler returns status code 12 (`UNIMPLEMENTED`),
> **not** `NOT_SERVING`. Check for `grpc.StatusOK` first, then inspect `message.status`
> only if the call itself succeeded.

---

### gRPC Server Reflection — Load Proto Definitions Dynamically  (k6 v0.49+)

When `.proto` files are not available at test time, use `reflect: true` in
`client.connect()` to load service definitions from the server's reflection endpoint.
This is useful for testing internal services where proto files are not checked into the
test repo.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/grpc-reflection.js — proto-less gRPC testing via server reflection
import grpc from "k6/net/grpc";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

const client = new grpc.Client();
// No client.load() needed when using reflection
// The server must implement grpc.reflection.v1alpha.ServerReflection

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    reflection_test: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 5,
      duration: "1m",
    },
  },
};

export function setup() {
  // reflect: true fetches service descriptors from the server
  client.connect(__ENV.GRPC_ADDR || "internal-api:50051", {
    plaintext: true,
    reflect: true,
    timeout: "10s",   // reflection load can be slow on large schemas
  });
}

export default function () {
  const res = client.invoke(
    "com.example.UserService/GetUser",
    { userId: `user-${__VU}` },
    {
      metadata: {
        authorization: [`Bearer ${__ENV.AUTH_TOKEN}`],
      },
    }
  );

  check(res, {
    "status OK":   (r) => r.status === grpc.StatusOK,
    "user found":  (r) => !!r.message?.userId,
  });

  sleep(1);
}

export function teardown() {
  client.close();
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #115:** Server reflection descriptors are fetched **once per
> `client.connect()` call**. If the service schema changes mid-test (rolling deploy), k6
> does not re-fetch the descriptors — calls to new or renamed methods will fail with
> `UNIMPLEMENTED`. For rolling deploy tests, reconnect in `setup()` after a short wait for
> the deployment to stabilize.

---

### `k6/html` — jQuery-Like Response Body Parsing

For testing server-rendered HTML pages or scraping CSRF tokens from login forms, the
`k6/html` module provides a `parseHTML()` function that returns a jQuery-like `Selection`
object, enabling familiar CSS selector queries without a real browser.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/html-form-scrape.js — scrape CSRF token from login form
import http           from "k6/http";
import { parseHTML }  from "k6/html";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    form_login: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 20,
      duration: "3m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<600"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.005"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  // ── Step 1: GET login page and scrape CSRF token ──────────────────────────
  const loginPageRes = http.get(`${__ENV.APP_URL}/login`);

  check(loginPageRes, { "login page loaded": (r) => r.status === 200 });

  const doc       = parseHTML(loginPageRes.body);
  const csrfToken = doc.find('input[name="_csrf"]').first().attr("value");
  const formAction = doc.find("form#login-form").attr("action") || "/login";

  if (!csrfToken) {
    console.error(`VU ${__VU}: CSRF token not found — login page may have changed`);
    return;
  }

  // ── Step 2: POST credentials with scraped CSRF token ─────────────────────
  const loginRes = http.post(
    `${__ENV.APP_URL}${formAction}`,
    {
      username:  `user${__VU}@example.com`,
      password:  __ENV.TEST_PASSWORD || "password123",
      _csrf:     csrfToken,
    },
    {
      headers:   { "Content-Type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" },
      redirects: 0,   // capture the redirect, don't follow automatically
    }
  );

  check(loginRes, {
    "redirect to dashboard": (r) => r.status === 302 || r.status === 303,
    "location header set":   (r) => r.headers["Location"]?.includes("/dashboard"),
  });

  // ── Step 3: Assert meta tag content in page response ─────────────────────
  if (loginRes.status === 200) {
    const body        = parseHTML(loginRes.body);
    const pageTitle   = body.find("title").text();
    const errorMsg    = body.find(".alert-danger").text();
    check(null, {
      "no error message": () => !errorMsg.trim(),
      "correct page title": () => pageTitle.includes("Login"),
    });
  }

  sleep(Math.random() * 2 + 1);
}
```

**`Selection` API quick reference:**

| Method | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `find(selector)` | Query descendants by CSS selector |
| `first()` / `last()` / `eq(n)` | Access first/last/nth element |
| `attr(name)` | Get attribute value |
| `text()` | Get combined text content |
| `html()` | Get inner HTML |
| `val()` | Get input value |
| `each(fn)` | Iterate over matched elements |
| `size()` | Number of matched elements |
| `children()` / `parent()` | DOM traversal |

> **[community] Gotcha #116:** `parseHTML()` operates on a **static snapshot** of the
> response body — there is no JavaScript execution, DOM mutation, or dynamic content
> loading. CSRF tokens injected by client-side JavaScript after page load cannot be scraped
> this way. If the CSRF token is set dynamically, use the k6 browser module instead.

---

### `SharedArray` — Memory-Efficient Large Dataset Pattern  (Anti-Pattern: `.filter()/.map()` in `default()`)

`SharedArray` stores data once in memory and exposes read-only views to all VUs. The
critical anti-pattern is calling array methods like `.filter()` or `.map()` on a
`SharedArray` inside `default()` — this materializes a full regular array per VU per
iteration, destroying the memory benefit.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/shared-array-efficient.js — correct SharedArray usage patterns
import { SharedArray } from "k6/data";
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

// ── CORRECT: transform/filter in the constructor (runs once, shared) ─────────
const USERS = new SharedArray("users", () => {
  const raw = JSON.parse(open("./data/users.json"));
  // Filter and map INSIDE the constructor — runs once for all VUs
  return raw
    .filter((u) => u.active && u.tier === "premium")  // ✓ runs once
    .map((u) => ({ email: u.email, token: u.auth_token }));  // ✓ runs once
});

// ── CORRECT: precompute index maps in init context ────────────────────────────
// Group by region in init context so VUs don't do it every iteration
const USERS_BY_REGION = (() => {
  const map = {};
  for (let i = 0; i < USERS.length; i++) {
    const region = USERS[i].region ?? "default";
    if (!map[region]) map[region] = [];
    map[region].push(i);  // store indices, not copies
  }
  return map;
})();

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    premium_load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "1m", target: 100 },
        { duration: "3m", target: 100 },
        { duration: "30s", target: 0 },
      ],
    },
  },
};

export default function () {
  // ── CORRECT: index directly — SharedArray element access is O(1) ──────────
  const user = USERS[__VU % USERS.length];

  // ── WRONG (don't do this in default()): ───────────────────────────────────
  // const filtered = USERS.filter(u => u.region === 'eu');  // ← copies all data!
  // const mapped   = USERS.map(u => u.email);                // ← copies all data!

  const res = http.get(
    `${__ENV.API_URL}/dashboard`,
    { headers: { Authorization: `Bearer ${user.token}` } }
  );

  check(res, {
    "dashboard loaded": (r) => r.status === 200,
    "has premium data": (r) => r.json("tier") === "premium",
  });

  sleep(1);
}
```

**Memory usage benchmarks (from official docs):**

| Array size | Regular Array (100 VUs) | SharedArray (100 VUs) |
|------------|------------------------|----------------------|
| 1,000 rows | ~50 MB | ~40 MB (minimal gain) |
| 10,000 rows | ~500 MB | ~80 MB |
| 100,000 rows | ~8.3–9.1 GB | ~238–275 MB |

> **[community] Gotcha #117:** **Never return a `SharedArray` from `setup()`**.
> k6 serializes the `setup()` return value and passes it to each VU through a JSON
> marshal/unmarshal cycle, which creates a full copy of the data in each VU's heap —
> completely negating the `SharedArray` memory savings. Instead, declare `SharedArray`
> in the **init context** (module scope) where it is automatically shared.

---

### Open Model Executor (`constant-arrival-rate`) — Avoiding Coordinated Omission

The **closed model** (constant-vus, ramping-vus) couples arrival rate to response time:
when the system slows down, VUs wait longer and fewer requests per second are generated —
masking the true capacity limit. Use `constant-arrival-rate` or `ramping-arrival-rate`
(open model) to maintain a fixed request rate regardless of system response time.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/open-model-load.js — arrival rate executor avoids coordinated omission
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend }         from "k6/metrics";

const waitTime = new Trend("iteration_wait_ms", true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    // ── Open model: target 200 req/s steady state ──────────────────────────
    api_load: {
      executor:        "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:             200,           // 200 iterations per timeUnit
      timeUnit:        "1s",           // = 200 req/s
      duration:        "10m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 100,
      maxVUs:          500,            // k6 will spawn more VUs if needed
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500", "p(99)<2000"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.005"],
    // If dropped_iterations > 0, maxVUs is too low
    dropped_iterations: ["count<100"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const iterStart = Date.now();

  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/products`, {
    timeout: "10s",
  });

  check(res, {
    "status 200": (r) => r.status === 200,
  });

  // Measure how long the default() function took in total
  waitTime.add(Date.now() - iterStart);

  // NOTE: sleep() is NOT used in arrival-rate scenarios.
  // The executor controls timing — sleep() would delay the iteration start
  // for the NEXT VU only if all VUs are busy (visible as dropped_iterations).
}
```

**Model comparison:**

| Property | Closed model (constant-vus) | Open model (constant-arrival-rate) |
|----------|----------------------------|------------------------------------|
| Load shape | Fixed concurrent users | Fixed arrival rate (req/s) |
| Coordinated omission | Yes — load drops when system slows | No — rate maintained independently |
| Modeling | Browser-like: users wait for response | API/backend: independent request streams |
| VU count | Fixed | Auto-scales up to `maxVUs` |
| `sleep()` role | Controls think time between requests | Usually omitted — executor controls pacing |

> **[community] Gotcha #118:** With `constant-arrival-rate`, when `preAllocatedVUs` is
> exhausted and k6 cannot spawn new VUs up to `maxVUs` fast enough, iterations are
> **dropped** (counted in `dropped_iterations` metric). A rising `dropped_iterations` count
> means your VU pool is undersized for the target rate, not that the system under test is
> failing. Set `maxVUs` to at least 3× `preAllocatedVUs` and add a
> `"dropped_iterations count<100"` threshold.

---

### Multi-Connection WebSocket Per VU (Global Event Loop)  (k6 `k6/websockets` stable)

The stable `k6/websockets` module uses a **global event loop** (unlike the legacy
`k6/ws` module which used a per-connection local loop). This allows a single VU to hold
multiple concurrent WebSocket connections — useful for chat, multiplayer, or pubsub testing.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/websocket-multi-conn.js — multiple WS connections per VU
import { WebSocket } from "k6/websockets";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Counter }   from "k6/metrics";

const msgsReceived = new Counter("ws_msgs_received");
const msgsDropped  = new Counter("ws_msgs_dropped");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    chat_load: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus: 20,
      duration: "5m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    ws_msgs_received: ["count>1000"],
    ws_msgs_dropped:  ["count<10"],
  },
};

export default async function () {
  const BASE   = __ENV.WS_URL || "wss://api.example.com/ws";
  const userId = `user-${__VU}`;

  // ── Open two connections per VU (e.g., chat + notifications channel) ──────
  let chatDone  = false;
  let notifDone = false;

  const chat = new WebSocket(`${BASE}/chat?userId=${userId}`);
  chat.addEventListener("open", () => {
    chat.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "join", room: "general" }));
  });
  chat.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    msgsReceived.add(1);
    const msg = JSON.parse(e.data);
    if (msg.type === "pong") chatDone = true;
  });
  chat.addEventListener("error", () => msgsDropped.add(1));

  const notif = new WebSocket(`${BASE}/notifications?userId=${userId}`);
  notif.addEventListener("open", () => {
    notif.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "subscribe", topics: ["orders", "promotions"] }));
  });
  notif.addEventListener("message", (e) => {
    msgsReceived.add(1);
    const msg = JSON.parse(e.data);
    if (msg.type === "ack") notifDone = true;
  });
  notif.addEventListener("error", () => msgsDropped.add(1));

  // ── Poll until both connections receive their ack messages or timeout ──────
  const DEADLINE = Date.now() + 15_000;
  while ((!chatDone || !notifDone) && Date.now() < DEADLINE) {
    // Trigger the global event loop to process pending WS events
    sleep(0.05);
  }

  chat.send(JSON.stringify({ type: "ping" }));
  sleep(0.2);

  chat.close(1000, "test done");
  notif.close(1000, "test done");

  check(chatDone,  { "chat ack received":  Boolean });
  check(notifDone, { "notif ack received": Boolean });

  sleep(1);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #119:** The `k6/websockets` module **does NOT share a single TCP
> connection between VUs**. Each VU manages its own set of connections in the global event
> loop. The "global" event loop means a single VU can multiplex events from multiple
> connections — it does NOT mean VUs share connections. If you have 50 VUs each with 2
> connections, k6 opens 100 WebSocket connections total.

---

### `xk6-disruptor` — Fault Injection Alongside Load Testing

`xk6-disruptor` injects HTTP/gRPC faults (latency, error rate) into Kubernetes Services or
Pods while k6 runs a concurrent load test. This lets you verify SLOs under failure
conditions in the same test run. It requires a Kubernetes cluster and is typically run via
`k6-operator`.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/disruptor-chaos.js — combined load + fault injection
// Prerequisites: xk6-disruptor extension, Kubernetes cluster, appropriate RBAC
// Run: K6_KUBECONFIG=~/.kube/config k6 run --out cloud disruptor-chaos.js
import http                        from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep, group }      from "k6";
import { ServiceDisruptor }         from "k6/x/disruptor";
import { Trend, Counter }           from "k6/metrics";

const orderApiDuration = new Trend("order_api_duration_ms", true);
const orderApiErrors   = new Counter("order_api_errors");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    // ── Steady load throughout the test ─────────────────────────────────────
    load: {
      executor: "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:      50,
      timeUnit: "1s",
      duration: "6m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 30,
      maxVUs: 100,
    },
    // ── Fault injection: runs once at t=60s, injects for 120s ───────────────
    inject_faults: {
      executor:  "shared-iterations",
      vus:        1,
      iterations: 1,
      startTime: "60s",
      exec:      "injectFaults",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    // During faults, 99th percentile must stay under 3 s
    "order_api_duration_ms{scenario:load}": ["p(99)<3000"],
    // Error rate may spike but must recover after faults clear
    "order_api_errors": ["count<500"],
  },
};

// ── Fault injection function ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
export function injectFaults() {
  const disruptor = new ServiceDisruptor("order-service", "production");
  disruptor.injectHTTPFaults(
    {
      averageDelay: "100ms",  // add 100 ms latency to all requests
      errorRate:     0.05,    // 5% of requests return errors
      errorCode:     503,
    },
    "120s",  // inject for 2 minutes
  );
  console.log("Fault injection complete — faults cleared");
}

// ── Load function ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
export default function () {
  group("order flow", () => {
    const t0  = Date.now();
    const res = http.post(
      `${__ENV.API_URL}/orders`,
      JSON.stringify({ productId: `PROD-${__VU}`, qty: 1 }),
      { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
    );

    orderApiDuration.add(Date.now() - t0);

    const ok = check(res, {
      "order accepted": (r) => r.status === 201 || r.status === 503,
    });

    if (!ok) orderApiErrors.add(1);
  });

  sleep(0.1);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #120:** `xk6-disruptor` requires the **`xk6-disruptor` binary** to
> be built into your k6 binary — it is not available in the standard k6 distribution.
> Build with `xk6 build --with github.com/grafana/xk6-disruptor`. The extension also
> requires Kubernetes RBAC permissions for the `xk6-disruptor-agent` DaemonSet to run on
> target nodes. Missing RBAC is the most common cause of `ServiceDisruptor` initialization
> failures.

### `page.waitForResponse()` — SPA API Response Interception in Browser Tests  (k6 v1.4+)

`page.waitForResponse()` blocks until a network response matching a URL pattern or
predicate is received. It is essential for SPAs where UI updates are driven by background
API calls — without it, assertions on DOM state race against the network.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/browser-spa-response.js — wait for API response before asserting UI
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check }   from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    spa_test: {
      executor:   "shared-iterations",
      vus:         2,
      iterations: 10,
      options: { browser: { type: "chromium" } },
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    browser_http_req_duration: ["p(95)<3000"],
    browser_web_vital_lcp:     ["p(75)<2500"],
  },
};

export default async function () {
  const page = await browser.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto(`${__ENV.APP_URL}/catalog`, { waitUntil: "domcontentloaded" });

    // ── Set up response waiter BEFORE triggering the action ─────────────────
    // waitForResponse() must be started before the action that triggers the request
    const productApiResponse = page.waitForResponse(
      (res) =>
        res.url().includes("/api/products") &&
        res.status() === 200,
      { timeout: 10_000 }
    );

    // Trigger an action that fires the API call
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Load More" }).click();

    // ── Await the response — assertion deferred until network resolves ────────
    const apiRes = await productApiResponse;

    check(apiRes, {
      "products API returned 200":  (r) => r.status() === 200,
      "content type is JSON":       (r) => r.headers()["content-type"]?.includes("application/json"),
    });

    // ── Wait for DOM to reflect the new data ─────────────────────────────────
    await page.getByTestId("product-list").waitFor({ state: "visible", timeout: 5_000 });

    const productCount = await page.getByTestId("product-card").count();
    check(productCount, {
      "products rendered": (n) => n > 0,
    });
  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #121:** `page.waitForResponse()` must be **set up before** the
> action that triggers the network request. If you call `waitForResponse()` after the
> action (e.g., after `click()`), the response may arrive before the listener is registered
> and `waitForResponse()` will hang until timeout. Always follow the pattern:
> `const waiter = page.waitForResponse(pred); await action(); const res = await waiter;`

---

### `locator.filter()` + `locator.all()` — Collection Assertions in Browser Tests  (k6 v1.4+)

`locator.filter()` narrows a locator to elements matching additional criteria, and
`locator.all()` resolves the locator to an array of element snapshots. Together they
enable iterative assertions over lists without rigid index coupling.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/browser-collection-assert.js — filter and iterate over locator collections
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check }   from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    list_test: {
      executor:   "shared-iterations",
      vus:         1,
      iterations:  5,
      options: { browser: { type: "chromium" } },
    },
  },
};

export default async function () {
  const page = await browser.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto(`${__ENV.APP_URL}/orders`, { waitUntil: "networkidle" });

    // ── All table rows ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    const rows = page.getByRole("row");

    // ── Filter to only "pending" status rows ─────────────────────────────────
    const pendingRows = rows.filter({ hasText: "Pending" });
    const pendingCount = await pendingRows.count();

    check(pendingCount, { "pending orders visible": (n) => n >= 0 });

    // ── Resolve to array and iterate ──────────────────────────────────────────
    const rowArray = await pendingRows.all();

    let allHaveActionButton = true;
    for (const row of rowArray) {
      // Each element in the array is a Locator pointing to one matched element
      const cancelBtn = row.getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel" });
      const exists    = await cancelBtn.count();
      if (exists === 0) {
        allHaveActionButton = false;
        break;
      }
    }

    check(allHaveActionButton, {
      "all pending rows have cancel button": Boolean,
    });

    // ── nth() for index-based access ──────────────────────────────────────────
    if (pendingCount > 0) {
      const firstPendingOrderId = await pendingRows.nth(0)
        .getByTestId("order-id")
        .textContent();

      check(firstPendingOrderId, {
        "first pending order has ID": (id) => !!id && id.length > 0,
      });
    }
  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #122:** `locator.all()` returns a **snapshot** of matched elements
> at the time of the call. If the DOM updates after `all()` resolves (e.g., infinite scroll
> appends new rows), the returned array does NOT reflect the new elements. For dynamic lists,
> use `locator.count()` after each page update instead of caching the `all()` result.

---

### `--new-machine-readable-summary` + `handleSummary` — Programmatic CI Reporting  (k6 v1.5+)

The `--new-machine-readable-summary` flag emits a structured JSON summary to
`stdout` (instead of the human-readable table) for easy parsing in CI pipelines.
Pair it with `handleSummary()` to generate multiple artifact formats from a single run.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/ci-summary.js — machine-readable summary + multi-format output
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { htmlReport }   from "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/benc-uk/k6-reporter/main/dist/bundle.js";
import { textSummary }  from "https://jslib.k6.io/k6-summary/0.0.2/index.js";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    smoke: {
      executor:   "constant-vus",
      vus:         5,
      duration:   "30s",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/health`);
  check(res, { "health ok": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);
}

// ── handleSummary: write multiple output formats ──────────────────────────────
export function handleSummary(data) {
  // data.metrics, data.root_group, data.state are available here
  const passed = !Object.values(data.metrics).some(
    (m) => m.thresholds && Object.values(m.thresholds).some((t) => !t.ok)
  );

  const ciAnnotation = {
    passed,
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    exitCode:  passed ? 0 : 1,
    metrics: {
      p95Duration: data.metrics["http_req_duration"]?.values["p(95)"],
      errorRate:   data.metrics["http_req_failed"]?.values["rate"],
    },
  };

  return {
    // Human-readable text to stdout (standard k6 table format)
    "stdout":           textSummary(data, { indent: " ", enableColors: false }),
    // HTML report artifact (CI artifact upload)
    "report.html":      htmlReport(data),
    // Machine-readable JSON for CI parsing
    "ci-annotation.json": JSON.stringify(ciAnnotation, null, 2),
    // JUnit XML for test result integration
    "junit-report.xml": buildJUnitXml(data),
  };
}

function buildJUnitXml(data) {
  const ts = Object.entries(data.metrics).map(([name, metric]) => {
    const failed = metric.thresholds &&
      Object.entries(metric.thresholds).some(([expr, t]) => !t.ok)
        ? `<failure message="Threshold failed: ${name}">${name}</failure>`
        : "";
    return `<testcase name="${name}" classname="k6.thresholds" time="0">${failed}</testcase>`;
  }).join("\n  ");

  return `<?xml version="1.0"?><testsuite name="k6" tests="${Object.keys(data.metrics).length}">\n  ${ts}\n</testsuite>`;
}
```

**CI usage (GitHub Actions):**

```yaml
# .github/workflows/perf.yml
- name: Run k6 load test
  run: |
    k6 run \
      --new-machine-readable-summary \
      --summary-mode=no-thresholds \
      k6/scripts/ci-summary.js \
      2>&1 | tee k6-output.json

- name: Upload k6 HTML report
  uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
  if: always()
  with:
    name: k6-report
    path: |
      report.html
      ci-annotation.json
      junit-report.xml
```

> **[community] Gotcha #123:** `handleSummary()` is **not called** when a test is aborted
> mid-run (e.g., via `abortOnFail`, Ctrl+C, or a fatal error). If your CI pipeline depends
> on the summary JSON to determine pass/fail, use the k6 **exit code** as the primary
> signal and treat `handleSummary` artifacts as supplementary diagnostics only.

---

### Prometheus Remote Write — Native Histograms with Stale Markers  (k6 v1.x)

`K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true` maps each k6 Trend metric to a single
Prometheus Native Histogram, enabling high-fidelity `histogram_quantile()` queries without
pre-committing to percentile buckets. Requires Prometheus ≥ 2.40.0 with the
`--enable-feature=native-histograms` flag.

```bash
# docker-compose.yml excerpt (Prometheus with native histograms enabled)
# prometheus:
#   image: prom/prometheus:v2.52.0
#   command:
#     - "--enable-feature=native-histograms"
#     - "--web.enable-remote-write-receiver"

# k6 run command for native histogram output with stale markers:
K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL="http://localhost:9090/api/v1/write" \
K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true \
K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_STALE_MARKERS=true \
K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_PUSH_INTERVAL="5s" \
k6 run --out experimental-prometheus-rw script.js
```

```javascript
// k6/scripts/prom-native-hist.js — load test with native histogram output
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend }         from "k6/metrics";

// Custom trends — each maps to a separate native histogram in Prometheus
const checkoutDuration = new Trend("checkout_api_ms", true);
const searchDuration   = new Trend("search_api_ms",   true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    user_journey: {
      executor: "ramping-arrival-rate",
      startRate: 10,
      timeUnit:  "1s",
      stages: [
        { target: 100, duration: "5m" },
        { target: 100, duration: "10m" },
        { target: 0,   duration: "2m" },
      ],
      preAllocatedVUs: 50,
      maxVUs: 200,
    },
  },
  // Thresholds are also enforced locally — Prometheus is for dashboarding
  thresholds: {
    checkout_api_ms: ["p(95)<800"],
    search_api_ms:   ["p(95)<300"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  // Search
  const t0      = Date.now();
  const searchRes = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/search?q=laptop`, {
    tags: { endpoint: "search" },
  });
  searchDuration.add(Date.now() - t0);
  check(searchRes, { "search 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });

  // Checkout
  const t1          = Date.now();
  const checkoutRes = http.post(
    `${__ENV.API_URL}/checkout`,
    JSON.stringify({ items: ["LAPTOP-001"], coupon: null }),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, tags: { endpoint: "checkout" } }
  );
  checkoutDuration.add(Date.now() - t1);
  check(checkoutRes, { "checkout accepted": (r) => r.status === 201 || r.status === 200 });

  sleep(Math.random() + 0.5);
}
```

**PromQL queries for native histograms:**

```promql
# 95th percentile latency for checkout (last 5 min)
histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(k6_checkout_api_ms_bucket[5m]))

# 99th percentile for search over test duration
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by(le) (rate(k6_search_api_ms_bucket[2m])))

# Compare p90 vs p99 spread (wide spread = high variance in response times)
histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(k6_http_req_duration_ms_bucket[5m]))
  /
histogram_quantile(0.90, rate(k6_http_req_duration_ms_bucket[5m]))
```

> **[community] Gotcha #124:** `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_STALE_MARKERS=true` writes stale markers
> after the test ends so Prometheus stops extrapolating metrics. **Without stale markers**,
> Prometheus dashboards show the last metric value as "current" for up to 5 minutes after
> the test ends — making it look like load is still running. Always enable stale markers in
> CI to avoid false alarms in Grafana alert rules.

---

### k6 Web Dashboard — HTML Report Export for CI Artifacts  (k6 v1.x)

The built-in web dashboard generates an HTML report after test completion using
`K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT`. In CI, disable the HTTP server (`K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_PORT=-1`) to
prevent the process from hanging after the test ends.

```yaml
# .github/workflows/perf-dashboard.yml
name: Performance Test with Dashboard Report

on:
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "k6/**"
      - ".github/workflows/perf-dashboard.yml"

jobs:
  load-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install k6
        run: |
          sudo gpg -k
          sudo gpg --no-default-keyring --keyring /usr/share/keyrings/k6-archive-keyring.gpg \
            --keyserver hkp://keyserver.ubuntu.com:80 --recv-keys C5AD17C747E3415A3642D57D77C6C491D6AC1D69
          echo "deb [signed-by=/usr/share/keyrings/k6-archive-keyring.gpg] https://dl.k6.io/deb stable main" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/k6.list
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install k6

      - name: Run k6 with dashboard export
        env:
          K6_WEB_DASHBOARD: "true"
          K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_PORT: "-1"      # ← prevents CI hang
          K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT: "k6-report.html"
          API_URL: ${{ secrets.STAGING_API_URL }}
        run: k6 run k6/scripts/main.js

      - name: Upload performance report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: always()   # upload even on threshold failure
        with:
          name: k6-performance-report-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: k6-report.html
          retention-days: 30
```

```javascript
// k6/scripts/main.js — minimal script to pair with dashboard export above
import http             from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

export const options = {
  stages: [
    { duration: "1m", target: 20 },
    { duration: "3m", target: 20 },
    { duration: "30s", target: 0 },
  ],
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${__ENV.API_URL}/health`);
  check(res, { "ok": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);
}
```

> **[community] Gotcha #125:** `K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT` generates an HTML report
> **only if test duration exceeds 3× the dashboard aggregation period** (default: 30
> seconds for a 10-second period). A very short smoke test (< 30 s) produces an empty HTML
> file with no graphs. For CI smoke tests under 30 s, use `handleSummary` instead.

### `k6 new --template browser` — Browser Test Scaffolding  (k6 v1.x)

The `k6 new` command scaffolds a new test script. The `--template browser` flag generates
a browser automation template with the correct scenario options block and browser module
import, eliminating a common misconfiguration error (missing `options.browser.type`).

```bash
# Scaffold a new browser test
k6 new --template browser my-browser-test.js
# Output:
# k6/scripts/my-browser-test.js created

# Run the generated test
k6 run my-browser-test.js
```

The generated template structure:

```javascript
// Generated: my-browser-test.js — browser test scaffold (k6 new --template browser)
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check }   from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    ui: {
      executor: "shared-iterations",
      options: {
        browser: {
          type: "chromium",
        },
      },
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    checks: ["rate==1.0"],
  },
};

export default async function () {
  const page = await browser.newPage();

  try {
    await page.goto("https://quickpizza.grafana.com");

    await page.screenshot({ path: "screenshot.png" });

    check(page, {
      "title is QuickPizza": async (p) => (await p.title()) === "QuickPizza",
    });
  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

**Available templates:**

| Template | Use case |
|----------|----------|
| `--template browser` | Browser automation with `k6/browser` |
| `--template minimal` | HTTP test with basic check pattern |
| *(default)* | Full template with examples of all major APIs |

> **[community] Gotcha #126:** Browser tests require the `options.scenarios[*].options.browser.type`
> field to be set. **Omitting the `options` block** (or setting `browser.type` at the root
> `options` level instead of inside the scenario) causes k6 to run in protocol-only mode
> silently — the `browser` import is available but `browser.newPage()` throws
> `"browser not enabled for this scenario"`. Always use `k6 new --template browser` as
> the starting point to avoid this misconfiguration.

### `http.asyncRequest()` + `Promise.all` — True Concurrent HTTP Calls from One VU

`http.asyncRequest()` is the async variant of `http.request()`. It returns a `Promise<Response>`
and unlocks `Promise.all()` / `Promise.race()` concurrency within a single VU iteration.
This is the idiomatic way to fanout to multiple endpoints without spawning extra VUs.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/async-fanout.js — concurrent HTTP calls from one VU
import http              from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep }  from "k6";
import { Trend }         from "k6/metrics";

const fanoutDuration = new Trend("fanout_total_ms", true);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    fanout: { executor: "constant-vus", vus: 10, duration: "2m" },
  },
  thresholds: {
    fanout_total_ms: ["p(95)<300"],
  },
};

export default async function () {
  const start = Date.now();

  // Fire all three requests in parallel — no sequential blocking
  const [users, products, inventory] = await Promise.all([
    http.asyncRequest("GET", `${__ENV.API_URL}/users`),
    http.asyncRequest("GET", `${__ENV.API_URL}/products`),
    http.asyncRequest("GET", `${__ENV.API_URL}/inventory`),
  ]);

  fanoutDuration.add(Date.now() - start);

  check(users,     { "users 200":     (r) => r.status === 200 });
  check(products,  { "products 200":  (r) => r.status === 200 });
  check(inventory, { "inventory 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });

  sleep(0.5);
}
```

**When to use:** APIs that return independent data (sidebar widgets, dashboard cards,
microservice aggregation). Fan-out collapses wall-clock time per iteration from
`sum(latencies)` to `max(latencies)`.

**When NOT to use:** If you need to abort in-flight requests on first failure — there is
currently **no `abort()` mechanism** in `http.asyncRequest()`. All promises run to
completion even after `Promise.race()` resolves.

**Tradeoff:** Each unresolved promise still counts against VU iteration time. Profile with
and without to confirm expected throughput gains.

> **[official]** `http.asyncRequest has no current way to abort a request.` Unconsumed
> promises continue executing until the full async job queue drains, which can inflate
> iteration duration in `Promise.race()` patterns.

> **[community] Gotcha #127:** Mixing `async/await` default functions with synchronous
> `sleep()` calls at the end is safe, but calling `sleep()` **inside** an `await` chain
> can stall the event loop and cause misleading timing in the iteration. Place `sleep()`
> **after** the final `await` at the top level to get accurate inter-iteration pacing.
