## Cycle 31 — Community Gotchas

### Gotcha 97. `exec.scenario.iterationInTest` resets to 0 at the start of each NEW scenario run — it is NOT a global test-level counter  [community]

**WHY:** If you have two scenarios sharing a `SharedArray` and both use `exec.scenario.iterationInTest` as the index, both scenarios will start indexing from 0. This causes both scenarios to read the same rows from the array, defeating the purpose of unique dataset coverage. Use `exec.vu.idInTest` combined with a scenario-specific offset (derivable from `exec.scenario.name`) to produce globally unique indices across scenarios.

**Fix:** Pre-compute a per-scenario start offset in `setup()` and pass it via `data`; add `exec.scenario.iterationInTest` to the offset inside `default()`.

---

### Gotcha 98. `options.cloud.distribution` percentages must sum to exactly 100 — fractional rounding errors cause a validation error at run start  [community]

**WHY:** When distributing load across Grafana Cloud k6 zones (e.g., 33% US-East, 33% EU-West, 34% AP-Southeast), manually rounding percentages often produces totals of 99 or 101 due to floating-point representation. k6 Cloud validates the sum server-side and rejects the run with a cryptic "distribution percentages must sum to 100" error that does not hint at the rounding root cause.

**Fix:** Always make one zone absorb the remainder: compute N-1 zones as floor percentages and assign `100 - sum(others)` to the last zone explicitly.

---

### Gotcha 99. `page.waitForLoadState("networkidle")` can wait indefinitely on pages with polling endpoints or long-poll XHR  [community]

**WHY:** `networkidle` waits until there are no in-flight network requests for 500 ms. Pages with analytics beacons, chat widgets, or long-poll XHR never reach this state, causing your browser scenario to time out with a misleading "page did not reach networkidle" error. The actual page content was fully rendered seconds earlier.

**Fix:** Replace `waitForLoadState("networkidle")` with `waitForLoadState("domcontentloaded")` or a specific element locator assertion (`page.locator("#main-content").waitFor()`), which is both faster and semantically correct.

---

### Gotcha 100. `http.setResponseCallback()` is GLOBAL and PERMANENT for the VU's lifetime — calling it multiple times stacks callbacks rather than replacing them  [community]

**WHY:** Teams call `http.setResponseCallback(http.expectedStatuses(200, 201))` inside helper functions that are called on every iteration, expecting idempotent behavior. In reality each call ADDS a new callback to the chain; by iteration 100 the VU has 100 callbacks executing per response, causing dramatic performance degradation and incorrect `http_req_failed` accounting.

**Fix:** Call `http.setResponseCallback()` exactly once, at module scope (outside `default()`), so it executes once per VU initialization rather than per iteration.

---

### Gotcha 101. `k6/x/redis` and other xk6 extensions require a custom-built k6 binary — the official `k6` binary does not include them and will throw "unknown module" at runtime  [community]

**WHY:** The k6 extension ecosystem uses the `xk6` build system to compile Go plugins into a custom k6 binary. Developers who install k6 via `brew install k6` or the official GitHub release and then `import redis from "k6/x/redis"` get a runtime error that looks like a missing npm package, not a binary mismatch. CI pipelines that use the official Docker image `grafana/k6` are equally affected.

**Fix:** Use `xk6 build --with github.com/grafana/xk6-redis` to produce a custom binary, or use the `grafana/xk6-redis` Docker image. Document the required extensions in a `xk6.json` or `xk6-manifest.yaml` in the repo root.

---

### Gotcha 102. `browser.newContext()` created inside `default()` leaks if `ctx.close()` is not called in a `finally` block — even if `page.close()` is called  [community]

**WHY:** k6 browser contexts are independent browser profiles (cookies, storage, permissions). If an assertion inside `default()` throws before `ctx.close()`, the context remains open for the lifetime of the VU, accumulating open Chromium renderer processes. With 20 VUs running 50 iterations each, this can spawn hundreds of orphaned renderer processes, crashing the Chromium host and producing "target closed" errors on subsequent iterations.

**Fix:** Wrap all browser context usage in a `try/finally` block: `const ctx = browser.newContext(); try { ... } finally { await ctx.close(); }`. This mirrors the Playwright best practice for test isolation.

---

### Gotcha 103. `SharedArray` name must be unique across ALL scripts in a distributed k6 run — duplicate names cause the second definition to silently shadow the first  [community]

**WHY:** In a Grafana Cloud distributed run that loads multiple script files via `import`, two scripts that both declare `new SharedArray("users", ...)` will collide on the name "users". The second definition wins silently — no error is thrown — so one script ends up reading the other script's dataset. This is especially insidious in monorepo setups where multiple test files share a common `utils/data.js` helper.

**Fix:** Use fully-qualified, file-path-derived names for `SharedArray`: `new SharedArray("auth/users-v2", ...)` instead of generic names. Establish a naming convention (`<domain>/<dataset>-<version>`) enforced by a custom ESLint rule or CI grep check.

## Cycle 32 — 2026-05-14

### 16. `ramping-arrival-rate` with Dynamic Stage Targets via Environment Variables  [official]

**Description:** Hard-coding rate targets in `stages[]` makes scripts inflexible across environments and CI pipelines. Pull `startRate` and each stage target from `__ENV` so a single script serves smoke (low rate), regression (mid rate), and stress (high rate) runs without maintaining separate files.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/ramp-env-stages.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";

const START_RATE  = Number(__ENV.START_RATE  || "5");
const MID_RATE    = Number(__ENV.MID_RATE    || "50");
const PEAK_RATE   = Number(__ENV.PEAK_RATE   || "150");
const PREALLOCATE = Number(__ENV.PREALLOCATE || "30");
const MAX_VUS     = Number(__ENV.MAX_VUS     || "200");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    dynamic_ramp: {
      executor:        "ramping-arrival-rate",
      startRate:       START_RATE,
      timeUnit:        "1s",
      preAllocatedVUs: PREALLOCATE,
      maxVUs:          MAX_VUS,
      stages: [
        { duration: "1m",  target: MID_RATE  },
        { duration: "2m",  target: MID_RATE  },
        { duration: "1m",  target: PEAK_RATE },
        { duration: "2m",  target: PEAK_RATE },
        { duration: "30s", target: 0         },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration:  ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:    ["rate<0.01"],
    dropped_iterations: ["count<20"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items`);
  check(res, { "status 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });
}
```

**CLI usage:**
```bash
# Smoke
k6 run -e START_RATE=1 -e MID_RATE=5 -e PEAK_RATE=10 k6/scripts/ramp-env-stages.js

# Stress
k6 run -e START_RATE=10 -e MID_RATE=100 -e PEAK_RATE=300 -e MAX_VUS=500 k6/scripts/ramp-env-stages.js
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use when a single script must cover multiple test tiers in CI. Do NOT use when stages have complex conditional logic (e.g., different step durations per tier) — at that point separate scripts with a shared library is more maintainable. Named alternative: `conditional-scenario-profile` pattern using `PROFILES[__ENV.PROFILE]` (see Cycle 31, Pattern 14).

---

### 17. `per-vu-iterations` for Deterministic Data Migration Testing  [official]

**Description:** `per-vu-iterations` guarantees each VU runs exactly N iterations. Combined with `exec.vu.idInTest` as a deterministic shard key, it lets you partition a dataset so that every row is processed exactly once across all VUs — ideal for migration validation, seed-data ingestion, or one-time transformation pipelines.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/migration-test.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";
import { SharedArray } from "k6/data";
import exec from "k6/execution";

// Load the full migration dataset once — shared read-only across all VUs
const records = new SharedArray("migration-records", function () {
  return JSON.parse(open("./data/migration-records.json"));
  // e.g. 1000 records, 10 VUs → each VU gets 100 unique records
});

const VU_COUNT = Number(__ENV.VU_COUNT || "10");
const ITERS    = Math.ceil(records.length / VU_COUNT);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    migrate: {
      executor:    "per-vu-iterations",
      vus:         VU_COUNT,
      iterations:  ITERS,
      maxDuration: "10m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<2000"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.001"],
    checks:            ["rate>0.999"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  // Deterministic sharding: VU 1 gets rows 0..ITERS-1, VU 2 gets ITERS..2*ITERS-1, etc.
  const vuIndex   = exec.vu.idInTest - 1;  // 0-based
  const iterIndex = exec.vu.iterationInScenario;
  const recordIdx = vuIndex * ITERS + iterIndex;

  if (recordIdx >= records.length) return;  // last VU may have fewer records

  const record = records[recordIdx];
  const res = http.post(
    `${BASE}/api/migrate`,
    JSON.stringify(record),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, tags: { name: "POST /migrate" } }
  );
  check(res, {
    "migrated":  (r) => r.status === 200 || r.status === 201,
    "not 409":   (r) => r.status !== 409,  // no duplicate processing
  });
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use for one-shot processing pipelines where each record must be processed exactly once. Do NOT use for sustained performance testing where VU lifecycle and iteration count should be unbounded. Named alternative: `constant-arrival-rate` with a queue-drain approach via Redis `rpop` (requires `k6/x/redis`).

---

### 18. Prometheus Native Histogram Output with Stale Markers  [official]

**Description:** Exporting k6 `Trend` metrics as Prometheus native histograms (rather than pre-aggregated gauge sets) preserves quantile accuracy at query time. Enable stale markers so Prometheus correctly marks series as inactive when the test ends — preventing phantom data in dashboards after the test run completes.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/prom-native-hist.js
// Run with:
//   K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:9090/api/v1/write \
//   K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM=true \
//   K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_STALE_MARKERS=true \
//   K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS="p(50),p(90),p(95),p(99),min,max" \
//   k6 run --tag testid=cycle32-${CI_RUN_ID} --out experimental-prometheus-rw script.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend, Rate } from "k6/metrics";

const checkoutLatency = new Trend("checkout_latency_ms", true);
const paymentErrors   = new Rate("payment_error_rate");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    checkout_load: {
      executor: "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate: 50, timeUnit: "1s", duration: "3m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 30, maxVUs: 100,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    checkout_latency_ms: ["p(95)<800", "p(99)<1500"],
    payment_error_rate:  ["rate<0.01"],
    http_req_failed:     ["rate<0.01"],
  },
  // Global tag so all metrics share a testid — required for unique Prometheus series per run
  tags: { testid: __ENV.CI_RUN_ID || `local-${Date.now()}` },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.post(
    `${BASE}/api/checkout`,
    JSON.stringify({ item: "sku-001", qty: 1 }),
    { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" }, tags: { name: "POST /checkout" } }
  );
  checkoutLatency.add(res.timings.duration);
  paymentErrors.add(res.status >= 500 ? 1 : 0);
  check(res, {
    "checkout 201": (r) => r.status === 201,
    "has order id": (r) => r.json("id") !== undefined,
  });
  sleep(0.1);
}
```

**Key Prometheus env vars:**
| Variable | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_SERVER_URL` | Remote-write endpoint |
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_AS_NATIVE_HISTOGRAM` | Enable native histograms (Prometheus 2.40+) |
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_STALE_MARKERS` | Send STALE markers after test ends |
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS` | Pre-aggregated stats to also export (fallback) |
| `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_PUSH_INTERVAL` | How often to flush metrics (default: 5s) |

> **Tradeoff:** Use native histograms when you need dynamic quantile queries (`histogram_quantile(0.999, ...)`) rather than pre-baked p95/p99. Do NOT use native histograms with Prometheus older than 2.40 — they require opt-in feature flags on older versions. Named alternative: `K6_PROMETHEUS_RW_TREND_STATS=p(95),p(99)` which writes gauges instead of histograms.

---

### 19. OpenTelemetry Output with Service Resource Attributes  [official]

**Description:** k6's stable OpenTelemetry output (k6 v1.3+) exports metrics to any OTLP-compatible backend (Tempo, Jaeger, Grafana Cloud Traces). Enriching the resource attributes with service name, version, and test environment enables Grafana to correlate load test metrics with distributed traces from the same test run.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/otel-enriched.js
// Run with:
//   K6_OTEL_GRPC_EXPORTER_ENDPOINT=localhost:4317 \
//   K6_OTEL_METRIC_PREFIX=k6_ \
//   K6_OTEL_SERVICE_NAME=checkout-load-test \
//   K6_OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES="deployment.environment=staging,service.version=1.4.2" \
//   k6 run --out opentelemetry k6/scripts/otel-enriched.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend, Counter } from "k6/metrics";
import tempo from "https://jslib.k6.io/http-instrumentation-tempo/1.0.1/index.js";

// Auto-inject W3C trace context on every request — correlates with backend OTEL spans
tempo.instrumentHTTP({ propagator: "w3c" });

const apiLatency  = new Trend("api_latency_ms",  true);
const ordersTotal = new Counter("orders_created_total");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    traced_checkout: {
      executor: "constant-vus", vus: 10, duration: "2m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    api_latency_ms:  ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed: ["rate<0.01"],
  },
  tags: {
    environment: __ENV.TEST_ENV    || "staging",
    service:     "checkout",
    version:     __ENV.APP_VERSION || "unknown",
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.post(
    `${BASE}/api/orders`,
    JSON.stringify({ sku: "item-001", qty: 1 }),
    {
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      tags:    { name: "POST /api/orders" },
    }
  );
  apiLatency.add(res.timings.duration);
  if (res.status === 201) ordersTotal.add(1);
  check(res, {
    "order created": (r) => r.status === 201,
    "has order id":  (r) => r.json("id") !== undefined,
  });
  sleep(1);
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use OTEL output when your observability stack already centralizes traces and metrics in an OTLP-compatible backend — it avoids maintaining a separate Prometheus scrape endpoint. Do NOT use OTEL output in high-frequency tests (>10k RPS) without tuning `K6_OTEL_FLUSH_INTERVAL` — the default gRPC flush interval can cause memory accumulation in the k6 process under sustained high throughput. Named alternative: `--out influxdb` for teams running a local Grafana + InfluxDB stack.

### 20. Web Dashboard Real-Time Export to Self-Hosted HTML  [official]

**Description:** k6 v2.0 ships the web dashboard as a built-in binary feature (no `xk6-dashboard` extension required). Enable it with `K6_WEB_DASHBOARD=true` and export a portable HTML report at test end using `K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT`. The exported file contains all metrics, charts, and threshold results — sharable as a single self-contained file without a Grafana server.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/dashboard-export.js
// Run with:
//   K6_WEB_DASHBOARD=true \
//   K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT=results/dashboard.html \
//   k6 run k6/scripts/dashboard-export.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Trend, Rate, Counter } from "k6/metrics";

const pageLoadTime = new Trend("page_load_ms",     true);
const errorRate    = new Rate("request_error_rate");
const totalReqs    = new Counter("total_requests");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 20 },
        { duration: "2m",  target: 20 },
        { duration: "15s", target: 0  },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    page_load_ms:       ["p(95)<500"],
    request_error_rate: ["rate<0.01"],
    http_req_failed:    ["rate<0.01"],
  },
  tags: {
    environment: __ENV.TEST_ENV  || "staging",
    run_id:      __ENV.CI_RUN_ID || `local-${Date.now()}`,
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items`);
  pageLoadTime.add(res.timings.duration);
  errorRate.add(res.status >= 400 ? 1 : 0);
  totalReqs.add(1);
  check(res, { "status 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(0.5);
}
```

**Key web dashboard env vars:**
```bash
export K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_HOST=0.0.0.0      # bind to all interfaces (for remote CI access)
export K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_PORT=5665
export K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_OPEN=false         # suppress auto-open in headless CI
export K6_WEB_DASHBOARD_EXPORT=results/report.html
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use for local development, PR review demos, and stakeholder-facing reports where spinning up a Grafana stack is impractical. Do NOT use as a production monitoring replacement — the web dashboard does not persist history across runs or support alerting. Named alternative: `handleSummary` + `@benc-uk/k6-reporter` for a leaner static HTML summary without real-time charts.

---

### 21. `k6/secrets` Multi-Source Routing for Staging vs. Production  [official]

**Description:** k6 v1.4+ `k6/secrets` supports multiple named sources in a single run. Scripts use `secrets.source(id).get(name)` to route credential lookups to environment-specific sources — the same script securely accesses staging keys from a local mock and production keys from Vault without any code change between runs.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/multi-source-secrets.js
// Run staging:
//   k6 run \
//     --secret-source=mock=staging,api_key="staging-key-abc" \
//     --secret-source=url=https://vault.internal/v1/secret/prod=production \
//     k6/scripts/multi-source-secrets.js
import secrets from "k6/secrets";
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    authed_load: {
      executor: "constant-vus", vus: 10, duration: "1m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<400"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

const BASE          = __ENV.API_URL      || "http://localhost:3001";
const SECRET_SOURCE = __ENV.SECRET_SOURCE || "staging";  // "staging" | "production"

export default async function () {
  // Route to the correct source by environment — no credential in __ENV
  const apiKey = await secrets.source(SECRET_SOURCE).get("api_key");

  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/secure/data`, {
    headers: {
      "X-API-Key":      apiKey,  // value is ***SECRET_REDACTED*** in all logs
      "Content-Type":   "application/json",
    },
    tags: { name: "GET /secure/data" },
  });

  check(res, {
    "status 200": (r) => r.status === 200,
    "not 401":    (r) => r.status !== 401,
    "not 403":    (r) => r.status !== 403,
  });
  sleep(1);
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use when a single k6 script must target multiple environments from a shared CI pipeline without hardcoding credentials per environment. Do NOT use `secrets.source()` without verifying the source name exists at run time — a missing source throws immediately and aborts the test before any VUs start. Named alternative: `k6/secrets` default source (`await secrets.get("key")`) for single-environment scripts; `__ENV` for non-sensitive configuration.

---

### 22. `exec.test.fail()` for Non-Blocking Pre-Condition Assertions  [official]

**Description:** `exec.test.fail(message)` marks the test as failed (exit code 110) without stopping execution. Use it in smoke-check logic at the beginning of the first VU iteration to flag a broken environment while still collecting partial metric data — useful when you need diagnostics from a degraded run rather than an immediate hard stop.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/preflight-fail.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import exec from "k6/execution";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 20 },
        { duration: "2m",  target: 20 },
        { duration: "15s", target: 0  },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";
let preflightDone = false;

export default function () {
  // Pre-flight: only on the very first iteration of VU 1
  if (!preflightDone && exec.vu.idInTest === 1 && exec.vu.iterationInScenario === 0) {
    const healthRes = http.get(`${BASE}/api/health`);
    if (healthRes.status !== 200) {
      // Mark test failed but CONTINUE collecting metrics — do not abort
      exec.test.fail(
        `Pre-flight health check returned HTTP ${healthRes.status}. ` +
        `Metrics below reflect a degraded environment.`
      );
    }
    const versionRes = http.get(`${BASE}/api/version`);
    const version    = versionRes.json("version");
    if (__ENV.EXPECTED_VERSION && version !== __ENV.EXPECTED_VERSION) {
      exec.test.fail(`Version mismatch: expected ${__ENV.EXPECTED_VERSION}, got ${version}`);
    }
    preflightDone = true;
  }

  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items`);
  check(res, { "items 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);
}
```

**Exit code reference for test control:**
| Method | Exit code | Behavior |
|--------|-----------|----------|
| `exec.test.abort(msg)` | 108 | Stop immediately; `teardown()` still runs |
| `exec.test.fail(msg)` | 110 | Continue to completion; marks run as failed |
| Threshold breach | 99 | Fail after run; all metrics collected |

> **Tradeoff:** Use `exec.test.fail()` when partial metrics have diagnostic value even from a broken environment. Do NOT use it instead of `exec.test.abort()` when the broken pre-condition makes ALL subsequent metrics meaningless (e.g., auth completely down — every request will 401). Named alternative: `exec.test.abort()` for hard early-exit with meaningful error messaging.

---

### 23. `k6 inspect` + `k6 deps` in CI as Pre-Flight Validation Gates  [official]

**Description:** Run `k6 inspect` to validate script structure (scenario VU counts, executor types) and `k6 deps` (k6 v1.6+) to verify all required extensions are present in the binary — before spending minutes on an actual test run that would fail at startup. Gate CI pipelines on these checks so misconfigurations surface within seconds.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# k6/ci/preflight.sh — pre-flight validation for k6 scripts
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT="k6/scripts/validated-load.js"

# 1. Validate script structure — outputs JSON with scenario/VU/executor info
echo "=== k6 inspect ==="
k6 inspect --json "$SCRIPT" | tee /tmp/k6-inspect.json

# 2. Check max VUs stay within CI budget
MAX_VUS=$(jq '.maxVUs' /tmp/k6-inspect.json)
if [ "$MAX_VUS" -gt 200 ]; then
  echo "ERROR: Script requests $MAX_VUS VUs — CI budget is 200 VUs"
  exit 1
fi

# 3. Verify no missing extensions (k6 v1.6+)
echo "=== k6 deps ==="
k6 deps --json "$SCRIPT" | tee /tmp/k6-deps.json

if jq -e '.customBuildRequired == true' /tmp/k6-deps.json > /dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "ERROR: Script requires xk6 extensions not present in this k6 binary."
  echo "Required extensions:"
  jq '.extensions[]' /tmp/k6-deps.json
  exit 1
fi

echo "Pre-flight passed — proceed with test execution."
```

```javascript
// k6/scripts/validated-load.js — companion script for pre-flight example
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    api_load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 10 },
        { duration: "2m",  target: 50 },
        { duration: "15s", target: 0  },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<300"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items`);
  check(res, { "status 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });
  sleep(1);
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use in PR pipelines where script changes could silently break the test (wrong executor, too many VUs, missing extension). Do NOT run `k6 inspect` and `k6 deps` as blocking gates in production smoke test pipelines where startup speed is critical — save them for the CI PR check phase. Named alternative: JSON schema validation on the `options` export using a custom ESLint rule.

### 24. Kafka Message Producer Load Test with `xk6-kafka`  [community]

**Description:** The `xk6-kafka` extension (`github.com/mostafa/xk6-kafka`) enables k6 scripts to act as Kafka producers. This pattern tests the ingestion throughput of a Kafka-backed event streaming pipeline by measuring producer latency and topic saturation under load — a gap that pure HTTP load tests cannot fill.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/kafka-producer-load.js
// Requires: xk6 build --with github.com/mostafa/xk6-kafka
import { Writer, CODEC_GZIP } from "k6/x/kafka";
import { check } from "k6";
import { Counter, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const messagesProduced = new Counter("kafka_messages_produced");
const produceLatency   = new Trend("kafka_produce_latency_ms", true);

const writer = new Writer({
  brokers:         [__ENV.KAFKA_BROKER || "localhost:9092"],
  topic:           __ENV.KAFKA_TOPIC   || "load-test-events",
  compression:     CODEC_GZIP,
  autoCreateTopic: true,
});

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    kafka_load: {
      executor:        "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:            100,
      timeUnit:        "1s",
      duration:        "2m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 20,
      maxVUs:          60,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    kafka_produce_latency_ms: ["p(95)<200", "p(99)<500"],
    kafka_messages_produced:  ["count>100"],
  },
};

export default function () {
  const payload = JSON.stringify({
    eventId:   `evt-${__VU}-${__ITER}`,
    eventType: "order.created",
    timestamp: new Date().toISOString(),
    data:      { orderId: `ord-${__ITER}`, sku: "item-001", qty: 1 },
  });

  const startTime = Date.now();
  const error     = writer.produce({
    messages: [{
      key:   `key-${__VU}`,
      value: payload,
    }],
  });
  const elapsed = Date.now() - startTime;

  produceLatency.add(elapsed);
  check(error, { "no produce error": (e) => !e });
  if (!error) messagesProduced.add(1);
}

export function teardown() {
  writer.close();
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use when your SUT includes event-driven components (Kafka consumers, stream processors) that are not covered by HTTP load tests. Do NOT use this extension to test Kafka cluster performance in isolation — it tests the k6-to-Kafka producer path, not consumer lag or partition rebalancing. Named alternative: `xk6-mqtt` (`github.com/grafana/xk6-mqtt`) for MQTT-based IoT event pipelines.

### 25. Rate Limiting Validation — Asserting HTTP 429 Behavior  [community]

**Description:** Rate-limited APIs are a special case: 429 responses are expected and correct. The goal is to verify that: (1) the rate limiter activates at the right RPS, (2) `Retry-After` headers are present and accurate, and (3) the system recovers correctly once load drops. This requires a custom `Rate` metric to distinguish expected 429s from genuine failures.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/rate-limit-validation.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";
import { Rate, Counter, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const rateLimitedReqs = new Rate("rate_limited_rate");
const successReqs     = new Rate("success_rate");
const retryAfterMs    = new Trend("retry_after_ms",  true);
const rateLimitCount  = new Counter("rate_limit_hits");

// Tell k6 that 429 is expected — not a failure
http.setResponseCallback(
  http.expectedStatuses({ min: 200, max: 299 }, 429)
);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    // Phase 1: below rate limit (expect 0% 429)
    below_limit: {
      executor:        "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:            20,
      timeUnit:        "1s",
      duration:        "30s",
      preAllocatedVUs: 10,
      maxVUs:          30,
      exec:            "sendRequest",
      startTime:       "0s",
    },
    // Phase 2: above rate limit (expect >50% 429)
    above_limit: {
      executor:        "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:            200,
      timeUnit:        "1s",
      duration:        "30s",
      preAllocatedVUs: 30,
      maxVUs:          100,
      exec:            "sendRequest",
      startTime:       "45s",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    "success_rate{scenario:below_limit}":      ["rate>0.99"],
    "rate_limited_rate{scenario:above_limit}": ["rate>0.50"],
    "retry_after_ms":                          ["max<30000"],
    http_req_failed:                           ["rate<0.95"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export function sendRequest() {
  const res    = http.get(`${BASE}/api/data`, { tags: { name: "GET /api/data" } });
  const is429  = res.status === 429;

  rateLimitedReqs.add(is429 ? 1 : 0);
  successReqs.add(res.status >= 200 && res.status < 300 ? 1 : 0);

  if (is429) {
    rateLimitCount.add(1);
    const retryAfterHeader = res.headers["Retry-After"];
    if (retryAfterHeader) {
      retryAfterMs.add(Number(retryAfterHeader) * 1000);
      check(res, {
        "Retry-After present": () => true,
        "Retry-After <= 30s":  () => Number(retryAfterHeader) <= 30,
      });
    } else {
      check(res, { "Retry-After header missing (bug)": () => false });
    }
  }
  check(res, { "not 500": (r) => r.status < 500 });
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use to verify the rate limiter contract — correct 429 rate, correct headers, correct recovery. Do NOT conflate this with a standard load test: a high 429 rate is success, not failure. Named alternative: `xk6-disruptor` fault injection for testing rate-limiter bypass and circuit breaker behavior.

---

### 26. Streaming Incremental CSV Processing with `k6/experimental/streams`  [official]

**Description:** The `k6/experimental/streams` module provides a Node.js-compatible `ReadableStream` API. Use it to process very large CSV datasets (> 100 MB) incrementally without loading the full file into memory — each VU reads and processes one chunk at a time, making massive parameterized tests feasible on resource-constrained CI runners.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/stream-csv.js — line-by-line CSV via ReadableStream
import { open } from "k6/experimental/fs";
import { ReadableStream } from "k6/experimental/streams";
import http from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";
import { Counter } from "k6/metrics";

const processedRows = new Counter("csv_rows_processed");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    stream_load: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus:      5,
      duration: "3m",
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration:  ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:    ["rate<0.01"],
    csv_rows_processed: ["count>0"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default async function () {
  const file = await open("./data/large-users.csv");

  const stream = new ReadableStream({
    async pull(controller) {
      const buf       = new Uint8Array(4096);
      const bytesRead = await file.read(buf);
      if (bytesRead === null) {
        controller.close();
      } else {
        controller.enqueue(buf.subarray(0, bytesRead));
      }
    },
  });

  const reader    = stream.getReader();
  let   remainder = "";

  while (true) {
    const { done, value } = await reader.read();
    if (done) break;

    const chunk = remainder + new TextDecoder().decode(value);
    const lines = chunk.split("\n");
    remainder   = lines.pop() || "";  // last partial line carries over

    for (const line of lines) {
      if (!line.trim() || line.startsWith("email")) continue;  // skip header/empty
      const [email, password] = line.split(",");
      if (!email || !password) continue;

      const res = http.post(
        `${BASE}/api/auth/login`,
        JSON.stringify({ email: email.trim(), password: password.trim() }),
        { headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" } }
      );
      check(res, { "login ok": (r) => r.status === 200 });
      processedRows.add(1);
    }
  }
  reader.releaseLock();
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use for CSV files > 50 MB where `SharedArray` + papaparse would consume too much memory. Do NOT use `k6/experimental/streams` for small datasets (< 10 MB) — the async overhead adds complexity with no memory benefit. Named alternative: `k6/experimental/csv` native streaming parser, which provides a cleaner API with automatic row splitting.

---

### 27. Conditional Abort with `exec.test.abort()` on Business Metric Drift  [community]

**Description:** Beyond threshold-based `abortOnFail`, use `exec.test.abort()` inside `default()` to programmatically abort when a business metric drifts beyond a limit that thresholds cannot model — for example, if the order creation endpoint returns non-201 responses on every attempt for the first 30 iterations on VU 1, there is no value in running 10 more minutes.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/abort-on-drift.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import { Rate, Counter } from "k6/metrics";
import exec from "k6/execution";

const orderSuccess = new Rate("order_success_rate");
const totalOrders  = new Counter("total_orders");

// Per-VU sliding failure window — reset each iteration
let consecutiveFails = 0;
const MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILS = 10;

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    checkout: {
      executor:        "constant-arrival-rate",
      rate:            30,
      timeUnit:        "1s",
      duration:        "5m",
      preAllocatedVUs: 20,
      maxVUs:          60,
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    order_success_rate: ["rate>0.95"],
    http_req_failed:    ["rate<0.02"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  const res = http.post(
    `${BASE}/api/orders`,
    JSON.stringify({ sku: "item-001", qty: 1 }),
    {
      headers: { "Content-Type": "application/json" },
      tags:    { name: "POST /api/orders" },
    }
  );

  const succeeded = res.status === 201;
  orderSuccess.add(succeeded ? 1 : 0);
  if (succeeded) {
    totalOrders.add(1);
    consecutiveFails = 0;
  } else {
    consecutiveFails++;
  }

  check(res, {
    "order created": (r) => r.status === 201,
    "has order id":  (r) => r.status === 201 && r.json("id") !== undefined,
  });

  // Abort if sustained consecutive failures indicate the endpoint is completely broken
  if (consecutiveFails >= MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILS) {
    exec.test.abort(
      `VU ${exec.vu.idInTest}: ${MAX_CONSECUTIVE_FAILS} consecutive order failures. ` +
      `Endpoint appears non-functional. Aborting to prevent misleading metrics.`
    );
  }

  sleep(0.1);
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use programmatic abort when business-level failure modes occur early and extending the test produces only noise. Do NOT use `exec.test.abort()` for normal threshold-based gates — `abortOnFail: true` on a threshold is simpler and more reliable for metric-based gates. Named alternative: `exec.test.fail()` if you want to flag the failure but still collect full metrics to understand the degradation timeline.

---

### 28. `options.minIterationDuration` to Prevent Hot-Loop VUs  [official]

**Description:** `minIterationDuration` enforces a minimum wall-clock time per VU iteration. If the iteration completes faster than this value, the VU sleeps for the remainder. This is cleaner than manually calculating `sleep()` durations and survives response-time variability — if a normally 200 ms endpoint temporarily returns in 20 ms, the VU still waits the full minimum duration before looping.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/min-duration-load.js
import http from "k6/http";
import { check } from "k6";

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    paced_load: {
      executor: "constant-vus",
      vus:      30,
      duration: "2m",
    },
  },
  // Enforce 1-second minimum per iteration — equivalent to sleep(1) but adaptive:
  // if response takes 800 ms → VU sleeps 200 ms; if it takes 1200 ms → loops immediately
  minIterationDuration: "1s",
  thresholds: {
    http_req_duration: ["p(95)<500"],
    http_req_failed:   ["rate<0.01"],
  },
};

const BASE = __ENV.API_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default function () {
  // No sleep() needed — minIterationDuration handles think time automatically
  const listRes = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items`);
  check(listRes, { "list 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });

  if (listRes.status === 200) {
    const items = listRes.json("items") || [];
    if (items.length > 0) {
      // Conditional second request — variable work per iteration
      const item    = items[Math.floor(Math.random() * items.length)];
      const itemRes = http.get(`${BASE}/api/items/${item.id}`, {
        tags: { name: "GET /api/items/:id" },
      });
      check(itemRes, { "item detail 200": (r) => r.status === 200 });
    }
  }
  // No explicit sleep() — minIterationDuration pads to 1 s total regardless of branch taken
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use `minIterationDuration` over manual `sleep()` when your iteration has variable work (conditional API calls) or when you want to guarantee a throughput ceiling without recalculating sleep times after latency changes. Do NOT use it with arrival-rate executors — `minIterationDuration` and `constant-arrival-rate` conflict: the min duration can prevent VUs from accepting new iterations, causing dropped iterations. Named alternative: explicit `sleep(Math.max(0, targetDuration - elapsed))` for precise adaptive think time.

---

### 29. Browser CDP `page.evaluate()` for JavaScript Heap and DOM Metrics  [community]

**Description:** k6's browser module allows executing arbitrary JavaScript in the Chromium page context via `page.evaluate()`. Use it to measure JavaScript heap usage and DOM node count under load — surfacing bundle bloat regressions and memory leaks that only manifest when the page is served under concurrent backend traffic.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/browser-heap-analysis.js
import { browser } from "k6/browser";
import { check } from "k6";
import { Trend, Counter } from "k6/metrics";

const jsHeapUsed  = new Trend("js_heap_used_mb",  true);
const scriptCount = new Counter("script_tags_loaded");
const domNodes    = new Trend("dom_node_count",    false);

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    bundle_analysis: {
      executor:   "shared-iterations",
      vus:        2,
      iterations: 6,
      options:    { browser: { type: "chromium" } },
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    // Alert if JS heap > 50 MB — indicates memory leak or bundle regression
    "js_heap_used_mb": ["max<50"],
    // Alert if DOM node count > 1500 — indicates render bloat
    "dom_node_count":  ["max<1500"],
    checks:            ["rate==1.0"],
  },
};

const APP = __ENV.APP_URL || "http://localhost:3001";

export default async function () {
  const page = await browser.newPage();
  try {
    await page.goto(`${APP}/`);
    await page.waitForLoadState("networkidle");

    // Measure JS heap via performance.memory (Chrome-only API)
    const heapMB = await page.evaluate(() => {
      const mem = (window.performance as any).memory;
      return mem ? mem.usedJSHeapSize / (1024 * 1024) : 0;
    });
    jsHeapUsed.add(heapMB);

    // Count <script> tags to detect bundle splitting regressions
    const scripts = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.querySelectorAll("script[src]").length
    );
    scriptCount.add(scripts);

    // Count total DOM nodes — high counts slow down interaction
    const nodes = await page.evaluate(() =>
      document.querySelectorAll("*").length
    );
    domNodes.add(nodes);

    check(heapMB,  { "heap < 30 MB":      (h) => h < 30 });
    check(scripts, { "script tags <= 20": (s) => s <= 20 });

    await page.screenshot({ path: `results/heap-${__ITER}.png` });
  } finally {
    await page.close();
  }
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use for catching frontend regressions (bundle size growth, memory leaks, DOM bloat) that only appear when the page is served under backend load. Do NOT use for high-VU browser tests — `shared-iterations` with 2–5 VUs is appropriate; browser scenarios are expensive and heap measurement adds ~20 ms of JS evaluation overhead per iteration. Named alternative: Lighthouse CI for static bundle analysis without a running backend.

---

### 30. gRPC Health-Check Pre-Flight with Automatic Abort Gate  [official]

**Description:** Combine `client.healthCheck()` in `setup()` with `exec.test.abort()` as an early safety gate. This ensures no VUs are allocated and no load is generated against a service that is already down — preventing false "low throughput" results from appearing in dashboards when the root cause is infrastructure, not load.

```javascript
// k6/scripts/grpc-preflight-gate.js
import grpc from "k6/net/grpc";
import { check, sleep } from "k6";
import exec from "k6/execution";
import { Counter, Trend } from "k6/metrics";

const rpcLatency = new Trend("grpc_rpc_latency_ms", true);
const failedRPCs = new Counter("grpc_failed_rpcs");

const client = new grpc.Client();
client.load(["./proto"], "items.proto");

export const options = {
  scenarios: {
    grpc_load: {
      executor: "ramping-vus",
      stages: [
        { duration: "30s", target: 20 },
        { duration: "2m",  target: 20 },
        { duration: "15s", target: 0  },
      ],
    },
  },
  thresholds: {
    grpc_rpc_latency_ms: ["p(95)<200", "p(99)<500"],
    grpc_failed_rpcs:    ["count<10"],
    checks:              ["rate>0.99"],
  },
};

const TARGET = __ENV.GRPC_TARGET || "localhost:50051";

export function setup() {
  client.connect(TARGET, { plaintext: true, timeout: "5s" });

  const overall  = client.healthCheck();
  const specific = client.healthCheck("items.ItemService");

  check(overall,  { "server overall healthy":  (h) => h.status === grpc.HealthCheckServing });
  check(specific, { "ItemService healthy":      (h) => h.status === grpc.HealthCheckServing });

  if (overall.status !== grpc.HealthCheckServing) {
    exec.test.abort(
      `gRPC server UNHEALTHY at test start: status=${overall.status}. ` +
      `Fix the service before running load. No VUs will be started.`
    );
  }

  if (specific.status !== grpc.HealthCheckServing) {
    exec.test.abort(
      `ItemService UNHEALTHY: status=${specific.status}. ` +
      `Partial degradation detected — aborting to avoid misleading results.`
    );
  }

  client.close();
  return { targetHealthy: true };
}

export default function (data) {
  client.connect(TARGET, { plaintext: true });

  const startMs  = Date.now();
  const response = client.invoke(
    "items.ItemService/ListItems",
    { page: 1, pageSize: 20 },
    { metadata: { "x-request-id": `k6-${exec.vu.idInTest}-${__ITER}` } }
  );
  rpcLatency.add(Date.now() - startMs);

  if (!response || response.status !== grpc.StatusOK) {
    failedRPCs.add(1);
  }

  check(response, {
    "status OK":  (r) => r && r.status === grpc.StatusOK,
    "has items":  (r) => r.message && Array.isArray(r.message.items),
  });

  client.close();
  sleep(0.1);
}
```

> **Tradeoff:** Use the health-check gate pattern whenever testing gRPC services in CI — it prevents a class of false failures where the CI environment is broken rather than the code. Do NOT skip `client.close()` in `setup()` after the health check — leaving a persistent connection open in `setup()` prevents VU code from connecting in some gRPC implementations. Named alternative: `exec.test.fail()` if you want to collect partial metrics rather than hard-abort on a degraded health state.
